jobs.name: netbox-api-token-rotation
jobs.description:
Rotates the shared NetBox provisioning API token every 60 days using a 90-day NetBox v2 token and seven-day overlap.

The job preserves all sibling Vault fields, validates both credentials, records only safe provider IDs in lifecycle telemetry, and deletes only the recorded predecessor after revalidation.

Every daily no-op also reads the canonical Vault path and authenticates its exact active token against the registered provider probe.

The first provider mutation remains canary-gated with FORCE_ROTATION.

jobs.name: jobsearch-collect
jobs.description:
[Jobsearch] Collect

Daily discovery step of the Job Search Intelligence Platform (backlog 44). Polls each
watchlist company's public ATS boards + aggregators and pulls two mailboxes -
[private detail] and the item-71 boards box (LinkedIn/Indeed alert emails,
parsed as multi-posting digests) - files one markdown posting per new job under
jobsearch/postings/YYYY-MM/, resolves full descriptions (including the tiered
Enrich alerts stage), upserts found rows (dedup by url_hash),
and commits the new files to main. Ollama/Claude scoring is a separate job
(jobsearch-enrich).

Schedule: Daily, ~06:00 (cron('H 6 * * *')). Agent: jobsearch. On standardPipeline, notifyOn: 'failure'.

What it does

Stage | What it does, and why

Migrate DB | jobsearch-db-migrate.py applies pending schema migrations first (nothing else does), so a fresh DB does not fail with relation "postings" does not exist. Idempotent via schema_migrations; --dry-run lists pending (verifying 001 postings + 002 resume_hash/llm_spend) before applying. Every collect self-heals the schema.

Greenhouse | jobsearch-collect-greenhouse.py polls every watchlist.yml company with a Greenhouse board (no API key), upserts postings, and writes a markdown file per posting. Filing keys on file presence, not just new rows: any known posting whose .md is missing is re-filed from the live body and its extraction is reset (self-heals a run that upserted then died before commit). Reported as new/refiled/seen; --refile forces a full re-file. A single board's HTTP error is skipped, not fatal. Thin wrapper over the shared jobsearch_collect core + ATS registry.

Lever / Ashby | jobsearch-collect-lever.py / -ashby.py: same core, for the public Lever (api.lever.co) and Ashby ([private detail], isListed only) APIs; source = lever/ashby, boards from the lever:/ashby: watchlist keys, ~1s/board courtesy sleep. New files are committed by the shared commit stage. No-op until slugs are populated.

Adzuna | jobsearch-collect-adzuna.py: aggregator keyword search (source=adzuna), terms + Denver where from the adzuna: block in watchlist.yml, company read per result. Creds (app_id/app_key) from Vault [private detail] logs one line and no-ops if the secret is absent. ~1s between terms.

HN Who is hiring | jobsearch-collect-hn.py: aggregator (source=hn). Newest whoishiring "Who is hiring?" thread via the Firebase API; parses top-level comments (first line Company | Role | Location), files only remote-friendly ones; url = HN comment permalink (stable dedup). Best-effort parse of free text.

BuiltIn Colorado | jobsearch-collect-builtin.py: HTML-scraped aggregator (source=builtin), standalone (BuiltIn has no JSON ATS API) but reusing the shared url_hash/file_posting primitives. Cookie-free GET of [private detail]/jobs with a browser UA; terms from the builtin: watchlist block, paginated (per_page 25) to a page/request cap. Cards parsed by stable data-id anchors via a scoped regex (no bs4/lxml in the image). Fragile by nature, so rate-limited and fail-soft: ~2s between every request, 403/429/5xx and any layout change are soft (skip-and-continue, no-op with a clear log), so a site change never breaks collect. Death detection falls to URL liveness, not board-diff.

Mailbox | jobsearch-ingest-mailbox.py pulls two boxes: jobs@ (generic forwards, source=mailbox) and the item-71 boards box ([private detail], via linkedin@/indeed@). Mail from a [private detail]/[private detail] sender is routed through the allowlist alert parser -> MANY postings per email (source=linkedin_alert/indeed_alert, canonical URLs, cross-source dedup + "also seen on" sightings). Board sender with no cards -> Failed (raw kept); non-board mail -> generic path, so jobs@ is unchanged. The boards box fail-softs until Phase 0 provisions it. Unparseable generic mail is filed as Unknown (mailbox).

Fetch bodies | jobsearch-fetch-bodies.py: list-only sources (BuiltIn) file a stub body (no description on the search page), which scores low and would be prefiltered out of Claude scoring. For stub-bodied postings from a source with a registered detail-page extractor, GETs postings.url, extracts the description (BuiltIn: [private detail] JobPosting JSON-LD), rewrites the posting body and resets extraction so enrich/scoring see real text. Runs before commit (enrich is DB-only) so the real body is committed. Considerate + fail-soft: courtesy sleep, browser UA, 403/404/timeout leave the body as-is. Source-agnostic registry.

Enrich alerts | jobsearch-enrich-alerts.py ([private detail]): resolves the full JD for alert postings, tier by tier - Tier 1 ATS (follow the redirect chain; if it lands on greenhouse/lever/ashby, fetch via the existing collector API paths - the Indeed rc/clk path), Tier 2 LinkedIn guest page (unauthenticated, rate-limited <=1/8s and <=60/run, authwall-aware), Tier 3 snippet. On a full JD it rewrites the body, sets description_confidence=full, fills canonical_url, and resets extraction. Runs before commit (like Fetch bodies) and in H6 so the JD precedes the H7 Ollama extraction. Non-goal: never fetches [private detail] job pages. Per-job cache (alert_enrichment, migration 016); no-op until alert postings exist.

Commit new postings | gitCommitPush commits exactly the posting files just written (enumerated via git status) to main as jenkins-bot, with [skip ci] so it does not re-trigger. Postings are a record, not a proposal, so they bypass PR review like host manifests.

Check liveness | jobsearch-check-liveness.py death detection: closes postings no longer live (never deletes), recording closed_at/close_reason. Greenhouse/Lever/Ashby via board-diff (one fetch per board, same ATS registry as the collectors; a failed fetch never mass-closes); mailbox/other via rate-limited URL liveness (404/410 or redirect-to-careers-home only; 403/429/5xx treated as live). Closed postings drop out of the dashboard's current-opportunity views.

Detect reposts | jobsearch-detect-reposts.py links a posting to the prior closed posting it reposts (repost_of): same company, near-identical title (normalized or rapidfuzz >= 90), reappeared after the closure. Feeds the dashboard "repeat offenders" table and the high-fit table's repost flag. Idempotent; a genuine backfill can look like a repost, so it is a signal not a verdict.

Watchlist

The companies polled are jobsearch/watchlist.yml. Adding or retiring a company (or
its Greenhouse token) is a YAML edit only, no job change. Companies with board: null
are not collected here; they arrive via the mailbox or a Phase 2 collector.

Prereqs: Vault secrets [private detail] [private detail] and (for item-71 alert ingest, once Phase 0 is done) [private detail] the bot token [private detail] the jobsearch-agent image published to the Gitea registry; and jobsearch/postings/** on the jenkins-bot branch-protection push allowlist on main (same allowlist as host_vars/**), else the commit push is rejected. Item-71 alert ingest + the Enrich alerts stage are a no-op until Phase 0 provisions the boards mailbox - see docs/pipelines/jobsearch-collect.md.

Source: jobsearch/Jenkinsfile-collect (built on standardPipeline + gitCommitPush) | Runbook: docs/pipelines/jobsearch-collect.md | Managed in git - edit the file, not this box.

jobs.name: cityamble-app-emulator-check
jobs.description:
[CityAmble] App emulator check

Runs a debug APK of the CityAmble store app (trip-app) on a headless Android emulator on the build agent and checks that it opens the live site the way a person would. The APK comes from [CityAmble] App debug APK.

What it runs: fetches the APK of build APK_BUILD (default lastSuccessfulBuild) and checks its sha256. Then it boots the ci-pixel emulator with wiped data and installs the app. It runs the Maestro flows in trip-app/maestro in order: 01 launch, 02 city, 03 sign-in panel, 04 relaunch. Each routine flow is recorded on video and ends with a screenshot. Optional parameter CAPTURE_PLAY_LISTING (default false) drives a real guest setup and archives two raw 1080x1920 (9:16) screenshots: a populated day planner and its map. It restores the emulator's display size afterward. For the map image, a CDP check waits up to 90 seconds for a ready basemap and at least one stop marker before taking the final screenshot. Last, a CDP script attached to the app's web view checks document.title and the service worker. The emulator is always stopped at the end.

Results: Build Artifacts, emulator-check/. Start with summary.json (pass or fail per flow and for the web view). Then screenshots/, optional play-listing/01-day-planner.png and 02-map-planner.png, video/, maestro/ (JUnit XML and Maestro debug output), webview-check.json, logcat.txt and emulator.log. A failed flow does not stop the others.

Sign-in: flow 03 stops at the signed-out sign-in panel. The app loads the production site, which has no test account, and no real credential is used.

Trigger: queued by every green [CityAmble] App debug APK build with that build's number, or Build with Parameters. One build at a time. Keeps the last 10 builds. The Job DSL seed owns the parameters and these job settings; keep them there because pipeline property updates replace the whole job property set. Agent: android-build-01 (label android-build, needs /dev/kvm). Reads the Jenkins automation token from Vault ([private detail] only to download the APK.

jobs.name: cityamble-app-debug-apk
jobs.description:
[CityAmble] App debug APK

Builds a debug APK of the CityAmble store app (trip-app, the Capacitor shell that loads [private detail] from main, for the Android Studio emulator or for side-loading onto a phone. Package com.cityamble.app, named CityAmble, signed with the build agent's debug keystore.

What it runs: npm ci in trip-app, npx cap sync android (which must leave the committed project unchanged), then ./gradlew assembleDebug. It checks the APK's package and label, then archives it as cityamble-app-debug-<build>-<commit>.apk with a .sha256 file next to it. The Toolchain stage prints the debug keystore's SHA-1, which the Google Cloud Android OAuth client for debug builds needs.

Download: open a green build and click the .apk under Build Artifacts. Drag it onto a running Android Studio emulator to install it, or use adb install -r on a phone.

Trigger: manual, Build Now. A green build queues [CityAmble] App emulator check for its APK. One build at a time. Keeps the last 5 builds and their APKs. Agent: android-build-01 (label android-build: JDK 21 compiler for Capacitor 8, Node 22, Android SDK platform 36). No Vault read and no credentials.

jobs.name: firewall-baseline-windows
jobs.description:
[Security] Windows Firewall Baseline

Reconciles one Windows host against the committed firewall baseline: the three profiles enabled with
inbound set to block, plus the estate's own inbound allow rules (RDP, ICMP echo). Managed from source by
jenkins/Jenkinsfile-firewall-baseline-windows, which applies
playbooks/firewall-baseline-windows.yml and nothing else.

CHECK_ONLY is ticked by default: the run reports what would change and applies nothing.
Untick it only after a check run on that host looks right. One host per run, chosen from the allow list.

Member servers do not accept WinRM from the provisioner, so the build opens a WinRM rule for that exact
source on the target, runs, and removes it again, verifying both. Domain controllers skip that path.

Read side: scripts/firewall-inventory-windows.py, the fifth surface of
[Assurance] Estate-wide Drift and Source Assurance. Runbook:
docs/monitoring/firewall-inventory.md.

jobs.name: estate-kb-scan
jobs.description:
Estate Windows KB scan (weekly)

Report-only Windows patch-state visibility: which Security/Critical
KBs are missing on each Windows host. Runs ansible.windows.win_updates in
state: searched (search only, never install) across the fleet over the existing AD/WinRM path,
then emails a by-severity report. Remediation stays with the Tier-3 patch pipeline. [private detail] (Leg 2).
Runbook: docs/pipelines/estate-kb-scan.md.

Stage | What it does

Scan the Windows fleet for missing KBs | Render management-enabled HostManifests and resolve the complete estate_windows fleet (domain_controllers + windows_managed) → estate-scan/playbooks/estate-windows-kb-scan.yml searches each host for missing updates and writes a per-host result (WinRM, shared DC or per-host member-server Vault password) → estate-scan/scripts/estate_kb_scan.py classifies by category (Critical / Security / Other), aggregates per host + fleet, renders JSON + Markdown + the backup-digest-style HTML email → lands run coverage in security_scan_runs → archive + email. Existing agents retain their proved HTTP/5985 inventory settings; new managed members use HTTPS/5986. KB titles are untrusted data: escaped for the report, no execution path.

Schedule H 5 * * 1 (weekly, Monday). The emailed report is the success signal. Report-only: nothing is downloaded or installed. Fail-closed: a host the scan cannot reach is reported UNKNOWN (never patched-by-omission) and marks the build UNSTABLE; the report is still emailed. Severity is category-derived (Critical/Security Updates), not CVSS - the signal Windows Update itself provides.

jobs.name: jobsearch-enrich
jobs.description:
[Jobsearch] Enrich

Daily enrichment step of the Job Search Intelligence Platform (backlog 44). Local Ollama
extracts skills and a 0-10 relevance pre-score for each new posting, then Claude scores the
relevant, unscored postings against the master resume behind a fail-closed monthly credit
gate. DB-only; no git commit. A green build with 0 scored is normal (empty backlog,
Ollama down, or budget reached) - not a failure.

Schedule: Daily, ~07:00 (cron('H 7 * * *')), after collect. Agent: jobsearch. On standardPipeline, notifyOn: 'failure'.

What it does

Stage | What it does, and why

Migrate DB | jobsearch-db-migrate.py applies pending schema migrations before the stages below use them (idempotent; a no-op when up to date). Enrich runs this too - not just collect - because the Ghost sweep needs the Phase 3 lifecycle schema (migration 008); running migrate here makes enrich self-sufficient and orders it before the sweep, so a migrate-ordering race cannot crash the build.

Extract (Ollama) | jobsearch-extract-skills.py drains the extraction backlog against local Ollama (qwen2.5:7b), storing skills + a 0-10 relevance and setting prefiltered = relevance < 5. The Ollama box is a not-always-on gaming PC, so if it is unreachable the stage exits cleanly without burning retries; a poison posting is retried at most 3 times then left for the digest.

Parse salary | jobsearch-parse-salary.py parses a $-anchored comp range from each posting body (deterministic regex, no LLM), stores annualized salary_min/max + salary_currency + salary_period (hourly x 2080), and marks salary_parsed so each posting is processed once. Backfills unparsed postings and picks up new ones. CO Equal-Pay ranges make this high-yield.

Parse deadline | jobsearch-parse-deadline.py parses an application close date from the posting body into deadline_at (phrase-anchored, deterministic, no LLM; never guesses), for the digest deadline-nag. Idempotent via deadline_parsed.

Score (Claude) | jobsearch-score-fit.py scores relevance >= 5 unscored postings (default model claude-opus-4-8, structured JSON) into fit_scores + current_score. A per-posting scoring error is logged and skipped, never failing the run; it bumps scoring_attempts and after 3 attempts (matching extraction) the posting is dropped from scoring with a "giving up" WARN, so a poison posting is not retried forever. Claude scoring routes through the LiteLLM gateway on the per-consumer jobsearch virtual key ([private detail] step 6b); the credit gate is unchanged.

Ghost sweep | jobsearch-application.py --auto-ghost (Phase 3 lifecycle upkeep) flips applied/screening applications silent for 40 days to ghosted (reversible - a later transition overwrites it). DB-only, no Claude. Fails soft if the lifecycle schema (migration 008) is not applied yet, so it never tracebacks on a not-yet-migrated DB.

Cost control

The fail-closed credit gate sums the month's llm_spend against
monthly_budget_usd (Vault) and denies scoring when the budget is reached or
unreadable, re-checked before every posting. Every call records its cost and is capped by
max_tokens, so spend is bounded structurally. Raising the cap is a Vault edit,
not a code change.

Prereqs: Vault secrets [private detail] and [private detail] (API key + monthly_budget_usd); reachability to the Ollama host [private detail]:11434; the jobsearch-agent image.

jobs.name: provision
jobs.description:
[VM] Provision Linux

Self-service, approval-gated creation of a fully network-configured, monitored, self-documenting
Rocky Linux VM. The operator supplies a name, role, and flavor; the pipeline allocates an IP from
NetBox, picks a Proxmox node by live capacity, builds the VM with Terraform from a
shared cloud image, registers it in Zabbix with a per-host PSK, configures the OS with
Ansible, enrolls Wazuh, applies current security patches, verifies PBS backup coverage,
creates DNS records, and commits a host manifest to git. It exists
so Linux VM creation is one repeatable workflow instead of a dozen manual steps, and so a re-run
against an existing host is a safe reconcile rather than an accidental rebuild.

Schedule: On demand (Build with Parameters). Agent: provisioner pod for the full workflow, including DNS registration over WinRM to the DC.

What it does (stage by stage)

Stage | What it does, and why

Validate input | Trims and regex-checks VM_NAME, computes memory in MB. Fails fast before touching infrastructure so a bad name never becomes a workspace/manifest key.

Checkout | checkout scm - brings in Terraform, scripts, playbooks, and (critically) any existing host_vars/<name>.yml manifest on main, which drives replay mode below.

Allocate IP from NetBox | netbox-allocate-ip.py <ROLE> <name> (token from Vault [private detail] reserves the next free address in the role's prefix; the bare IP yields a collision-free VM ID (octet3×1000+octet4) and the gateway. NetBox is the IPAM source of truth.

Select Node | Replay-aware ([private detail]): if a manifest with a recorded spec.node already exists, that node is reused. If the first run created the VM but failed before writing its manifest, the live Proxmox node resolved before IP allocation is reused instead. Both paths skip pick-node, preventing an accidental destroy+recreate. Only a genuinely fresh VM runs pick-node.py <MEMORY_MB>.

Terraform Plan | Selects an existing per-VM workspace or records that this build created a new one against the Postgres backend; then plans the VM. It greps the plan for forces replacement/must be replaced and sets PLAN_REPLACES so the approval can red-flag a destructive plan.

Approval | HTML email to [private detail] and a manual gate. On a normal plan the button is Apply; on a forced-replacement plan the subject/banner turn red "DESTRUCTIVE" and the button becomes DESTROY & RECREATE so an existing host is never silently replaced. The gate has a 60-minute timeout: a fresh build releases its new IP on abort, while a resolved existing VM retains its reservation.

Terraform Apply | Applies the approved plan, runs clear-tags.py, and sets VM_CREATED=true - the flag that switches later failures to roll-forward (IP retained) rather than cleanup.

Register Zabbix | zabbix-register-host.py creates the host and a unique PSK stored at Vault [private detail]<host>, generated before configure so the agent comes up already trusted.

Configure (Ansible) | Waits for SSH, then configure-host.yml applies baseline, firewall, NTP, Zabbix, Alloy, automatic patching, and Wazuh. Zabbix PSK and Wazuh enrollment credentials come from Vault.

Configure CI runner (when CONFIG_PROFILE=ci-runner) | Runs configure-ci-runner.yml to install Docker + the gitea-runner and register it (token from [private detail] Runs after the base configure so the baseline is already in place; base provisions skip it.

Initial security patch | Installs current Red Hat security updates, including approved first-boot kernel work, reboots when required, and requires no reboot to remain pending.

Operational readiness | Fails closed unless hardening and management services pass, the Wazuh API reports the agent active in linux-servers, and an enabled Proxmox backup job covers the VM on pbs.

DNS Register (provisioner to DC over WinRM) | playbooks/register-dns.yml uses the dedicated Vault DNS credential to create the [private detail] A record and attempt the reverse PTR, reporting a missing reverse zone as an explicit skip ([private detail]). It also creates a [private detail] A record when PUBLISH_DNS is set. No static Windows Jenkins agent is required.

Write host manifest | Records patch, Wazuh, backup, and compliance policy in inventory/host_vars/<name>.yml, validates it, proves the scheduled patch job can render the host, then opens a jenkins-bot record PR and blocks until it is durably merged.

Abort/failure cleanup: before VM creation, the job releases an IP allocated for a fresh build and deletes only a Terraform workspace that the same build created. A live VM resolved during replay keeps its existing IP on every abort/failure path. Workspace cleanup selects default first and never uses -force, so Terraform refuses deletion if a partial apply left managed resources.

Parameters

Param | Meaning, default, consequence

VM_NAME | Hostname, no domain. Regex-validated. Becomes the Terraform workspace and manifest filename - re-using an existing name enters replay mode against that host.

ROLE | infra/control/ci → [private detail]10.x, kubernetes → .20, identity → .30, clients → .40. Chooses the VLAN/prefix NetBox allocates from.

CORES | 1 / 2 / 4 / 6 / 8 vCPU. Recorded in the manifest flavor.

MEMORY_GB | 1 / 2 / 4 / 6 / 8 / 12 GB. Converted to MB and used by pick-node for capacity fit.

DISK_GB | OS/root disk in GB ([private detail]); base-profile default 20; CONFIG_PROFILE=ci-runner requires at least 100 (choose 100, 160 or 200). The capacity check runs after checkout and before any allocation. Passed to terraform as disk_size_gb; cloud-init growpart grows the root partition + xfs to fill it on first boot. Recorded in the manifest flavor.

CONFIG_PROFILE | base (default) = firewall/ntp/zabbix only; ci-runner additionally installs Docker + a Gitea Actions runner ([private detail]). Gates the conditional runner stage.

PUBLISH_DNS | Default false. When true, also creates a public [private detail] A record in addition to the always-created [private detail] one.

Failure & rollback

post success: emails "VM Provisioned" to [private detail].
post failure: if the VM was not created (VM_CREATED != true), the reserved
NetBox IP is released (netbox-release-ip.py; [private detail] finding 2: a failed release logs a WARN and marks the build UNSTABLE, no longer silently swallowed) and the mail says nothing was
created. If the VM was created, the IP is retained and the mail tells the operator to
re-run the same VM_NAME to roll forward - releasing the IP would orphan a live VM.

Note: Re-running for an existing host enters replay mode (node pinned from the manifest, plan should show 0 to destroy). A plan containing forced replacement gets a red DESTROY & RECREATE approval banner - read it; approving deletes and rebuilds the VM.

Dev guardrail (ADR-0018): on the dev controller (CONTROLLER_ENV=dev) Terraform Apply is skipped (plan-only); set APPLY_ON_DEV=true to apply for real. Prod applies as normal.

Source: jenkins/Jenkinsfile-provision | Runbook: docs/pipelines/provision.md | Managed in git - edit the file, not this box.

jobs.name: zabbix-selfheal
jobs.description:
[Ops] Self-heal

Weekly Zabbix self-heal on a detect-then-approve model. It finds every red (unhealthy)
monitored host, classifies why (TLS/PSK mismatch, wrong interface IP, agent allowlist, unreachable),
and remediates - server-side fixes via the Zabbix API, agent-side fixes via Ansible - but
nothing is changed until a human approves. It exists to kill the recurring toil of Zabbix
agents drifting (IP changes, PSK mismatches) without handing automation a blank cheque to mutate
hosts; a person always sees the preview and clicks Heal first. Every action is recorded to the
Postgres heal_outcomes store for auditing.

Schedule: Weekly, Monday ~08:00 (cron('H 8 * * 1')); healing gated on approval. Also runnable on demand. Agent: agent none; all work runs on the provisioner pod (Windows hosts are healed remotely via Ansible WinRM - no Windows agent).

What it does (stage by stage)

Stage | What it does, and why

Detect | scripts/zabbix-selfheal.py --report - report-only, makes zero changes. It classifies each red interface, resolves a trusted [private detail]x.x IP (inventory first, DNS fallback), and writes the Linux/Windows heal queues + generated Ansible inventories. The report is captured and archived so the approver sees exactly what would happen.

Approve heal | Emails the full report to [private detail] as a styled HTML message with a "Review & approve" button that opens the input page directly ([private detail], matching the provisioning approval email), then blocks on Heal these hosts? (button Heal). This is the mandatory gate - abort here and no host is touched. The gate has a 30-minute timeout ([private detail]): no response aborts and nothing heals.

Heal Linux | Re-runs the engine without --report - this is what actually applies the server-side fixes (Zabbix interface IP corrections and PSK re-sync from Vault) and records outcomes to Postgres. Then ansible-playbook heal-zabbix-agents.yml against the generated Linux inventory fixes the agents.

Heal Windows | ansible-playbook heal-zabbix-agents-windows.yml against the generated Windows inventory (Ansible/Vault env, collections installed at runtime) remediates Windows agent PSK/config over WinRM.

What it heals (classification)

Class | Action (after approval)

PSK / TLS drift | Re-syncs the host object's TLS PSK from Vault (dual schema: psk or identity/key) via host.update.

IP drift | Corrects the Zabbix interface toward a trusted [private detail]x.x source (inventory, then DNS with a range guard). Untrusted/unknown IPs are left untouched.

Agent down / allowlist | Queues the Linux/Windows heal playbook against the generated inventory.

Parameters

None.

Failure & behavior

No post block; the only notification is the approval email. Aborting the gate stops the
build before any change. There is no rollback of applied heals. Outcome recording to Postgres/ChromaDB
is fire-and-forget - a store outage is swallowed as a warning and never fails a heal.

Note: Detect changes nothing - ALL fixes (including server-side IP/PSK) apply only after approval, in the Heal Linux re-run. The queue the approver reviewed is regenerated at heal time, so it could differ if state changed between detect and approve. Unattended, the gate blocks and nothing heals. This is Level 1 (classify + dispatch): it does NOT re-check host health afterward, so a green build does not prove the hosts actually recovered - check heal_outcomes when auditing.

Source: jenkins/Jenkinsfile-selfheal | Managed in git - edit the file, not this box.

jobs.name: noc-reconcile
jobs.description:
[Monitoring] NOC overview reconcile (dead-man switch)

Nightly drift check for the generated NOC overview dashboard ([private detail] phase 4, [private detail]).
Regenerates the overview from the tagged grafana/*.json and diffs it field by field
against the live dashboard fetched from Grafana by uid noc-overview: tiles, queries,
links, threshold steps, value mappings, stat options, the banner text and the dashboard-level
editable/templating/tags. On drift it sends 1 to a
Zabbix trapper item so a pre-created trigger raises a problem, and pushes the first few drift lines to a
second trapper item so the problem names the panel and the field that moved; on a clean match it sends
0. Same watch-the-truth pattern as [private detail]'s backup dead-man switch.

What it is really watching for: not a Grafana UI hand-edit. The hub is provisioned from a ConfigMap and carries editable: false, so Grafana refuses to save over it. The vector that bites is the live hub lagging the repo - the sync job is pollSCM('') nudged by notifyCommit, so a missing webhook means nothing fires on merge, and a stale board looks completely normal.

Trigger: cron('H 4 * * *') (nightly ~4am, after the RAG re-index and log triage). Agent: provisioner. On standardPipeline helpers (withLabVault, labNotify).

Green vs red: the build stays green once the drift value is sent (0 or 1) - the Zabbix trigger owns the drift alert, so drift is a monitored condition, not a flapping Jenkins result. The build goes red only on an operational failure (cannot regenerate, reach Grafana, or send to Zabbix), which means the overview went unchecked and must be fixed.

Alert mail ([private detail]): this job calls labNotify() bare, not through standardPipeline, so it uses labNotify's own changed-only repeat gate: a run that goes red mails once on the transition into failure, then suppresses the same "still failing" repeat every ~4am run until it recovers, at which point a single "FIXED (was failing)" mail goes out. A multi-night Grafana/Zabbix outage no longer mails every night.

Committed-not-applied. Does nothing until the operator (per docs/ci-cd/noc-overview-deploy.md) creates the read-only Grafana service-account token in Vault ([private detail] the two Zabbix trapper items (noc.overview.drift, noc.overview.drift.detail) and their three triggers, and sets GRAFANA_URL (the internal Grafana service, not the Cloudflare-fronted FQDN) and ZABBIX_SERVER. Until then a run fails loud, never a silent all-clear. One of the three triggers is nodata(...,26h): without it, this job going dark is indistinguishable from a hub in sync.

jobs.name: build-windows-templates
jobs.description:
[VM] Build Windows Templates

Weekly Packer rebuild of the Windows Server templates that the Windows provision pipeline clones
from. The hard problem it solves: a broken golden image would break every new VM, so the
job never touches the live template in place. Instead it uses a stage → build → verify
→ promote pattern - it builds into a non-live "staging" VMID with a neutral tag, and
the live os-* tag only moves to the new image after the build succeeds and is
verified. A failed OS keeps serving its previous template, so provisioning is never down.
[private detail] (pack G): the two OSes now build as a declarative matrix, one pod each,
concurrently, instead of one after the other.

Schedule: Weekly, Tuesdays ~13:00 (cron('H 13 * * 2')). Also runnable on demand. Before each OS, a backup-collision guard reads Proxmox's live backup schedule and refuses a start when any enabled vzdump falls inside the six-hour pipeline horizon; it also refuses while any backup task is already running. This covers the daily jobs without hard-coded timezone assumptions and follows future schedule changes automatically. Agent: Checkout and the summary email run on one Kubernetes pod; each OS is its own matrix cell with its OWN fresh pod on the packer-agent image, so both build at the same time - safe because each OS's Proxmox VMIDs are a disjoint pair (never the same VMID or lock). Vault AppRole injected into every pod from the jenkins-vault-approle secret. Options: 6-hour pipeline timeout (backstop), a per-build 150-minute timeout so one OS's overrun cannot starve the other cell ([private detail]), disableConcurrentBuilds (blocks two RUNS of this job, not the two cells within one run), keep 20 builds.

What it does (per OS: 2022-rdp, 2025)

Step | What it does, and why

Stage | promote-template.py stage/stagetag <os> pick the non-live VMID of the pair and a neutral staging tag. Building to the non-live slot is what keeps the live image untouched during the build.

Build | VMID_OVERRIDE=<staging> TAGS_OVERRIDE='<stagetag>' ./build-template.sh vars/<os>.pkrvars.hcl. The build script self-authenticates to Vault via the pod's AppRole and pulls Proxmox creds; its return code is captured.

Verify (parallel, [private detail]) | Two independent, dissimilar checks run as parallel branches - neither waits on the other. scan: promote-template.py verify <staging> asks the live Proxmox API whether the staging VMID is actually a template now (a build can exit 0 yet not have produced a valid image). offline tests: scripts/tests/test_promote_template_cleanup.py, a pure-Python, no-network regression check that the promotion tooling itself has not broken.

Promote / Cleanup | On build success AND both verify branches passing: promote-template.py promote swaps the tags (old live → previous, staging → live). On any failure: the live tag is left untouched and promote-template.py cleanup destroys the failed staging VM so next week's slot is clean.

All Proxmox/Packer logic lives in scripts/promote-template.py and
packer/build-template.sh (both runnable standalone); the Jenkinsfile only orchestrates
the matrix ([private detail]: one pod per OS, built concurrently, replacing the old sequential
for-loop) and emails the summary. There is no approval gate - it is scheduled and never touches the
live template except on success.

Parameters

None. The OS list (2022-rdp, 2025) is fixed in the pipeline.

Failure & result reporting

A single post always block sets the build FAILURE if nothing succeeded,
UNSTABLE if partial, green only if all OSes built, and emails a per-OS HTML result table
(green/red per OS) to [private detail]. Rollback is implicit and per-OS: on
failure the live tag never moves and the failed staging VM is auto-destroyed.

Timeout diagnostics: packer output goes to a per-build log on the agent
(/tmp/packer-build-<vmid>.log). On a build failure the script dumps the last ~40 lines
to the console; and if the build is interrupted (a stage/pipeline timeout or abort, where the
script is killed before it can), the stage's catch dumps that tail into the console - so a
"Timeout has been exceeded" email links a log that shows where packer stalled (ISO boot, WinRM
wait, or a provisioner) - and destroys the hung staging VM so it does not idle until next week.
No automatic retry: a timed-out build never promotes (containment is by design).

Note: Provisioning clones whatever tag is promoted, so a bad promote would propagate to every new VM - the verify gate exists precisely to prevent that. Green does not guarantee all-success: watch for UNSTABLE builds, which mean one OS failed and is still serving its previous template.

Dev guardrail (ADR-0018): this job has no plan/apply split, so on the dev controller (CONTROLLER_ENV=dev) the whole rebuild is skipped rather than degraded to plan-only. Every OS is reported SKIPPED, the build stays green, and no summary email is sent. Set APPLY_ON_DEV=true to build on dev for real. Prod rebuilds as normal.

jobs.name: dr-restore
jobs.description:
[DR] Weekly Restore-Verify

Each week this job live-fire restores a backup into a throwaway guest and proves it BOOTS to the
documented recovery scope,
then destroys it ([private detail]). It is the only thing in the estate that proves a backup
restores into a bootable guest with readable runtime and filesystem facts, not just that a backup ran. It closes the gap [private detail]
(chunk-verify is checksum-only, never proves a boot) and [private detail] (a silent backup outage) leave open,
and it backs the site hero claim "backups verified weekly, live-fire".

Trigger: weekly, Sunday
(cron('H H * * 0')). Agent: provisioner (PBS + PVE reach + python3). On
standardPipeline, notifyOn: 'failure' - a failed restore, a failed verify, or
a red chunk-verify gate pages; a green run stays quiet.

What it does (per run)

Step | What, and why

Pick | A monotonic run index (whole weeks since epoch) rotates through the complete critical-infra guest manifest; every run restore-verifies the picked guest from both nas-datastore and dr-datastore (ruling 5, weekly-both). The scheduled GUEST default is blank; an attended run can still pin a name or VMID for diagnosis.

Chunk-verify gate | Stage-1 gate ([private detail]). Confirm the latest PBS chunk-verify for that guest's backup group on that store is OK. A red or missing verify FAILS the run here, cheaply, before any scratch VM is created. Integrity first, then bootability.

Restore | qmrestore the latest recovery point to a reserved scratch VMID on the correct node - never a live VMID. The source node is resolved explicitly and the scratch VM is asserted to exist post-restore (defeats the wrong-node silent no-op, vault-restore-runbook Finding 3).

Boot fenced | Boot the scratch guest on an isolated bridge with no uplink (the 2026-07-18 fenced ruling), so a restored DC or Vault can never answer for or collide with the real one.

Verify | qga-audit-only-v1: boot, agent response, filesystem mount, OS facts, and guest time through read-only QGA Audit endpoints. ADR-0019 keeps guest-exec and guest-file-open blocked. Service reachability is not claimed here; it requires [private detail]'s probe on the isolated segment.

Record + report | Record pass/fail + which guest/store was exercised and email the report (band 3). The emailed report is the weekly success signal; a stale weekly restore is visible on the existing mail path (no new channel).

Teardown | Always. Destroy the scratch VM on every outcome (success or fail), so a crashed run never leaks a duplicate guest or a disk.

RUN_LIVE: ON by default (since
OPS-016, "make the claim true") - the real restore-verify, against real PBS/PVE, with the report
emailed rather than only rendered; it requires NODE + FENCED_BRIDGE, both
defaulted to the deliberately coupled, rerun-12-proven pair (pve4 / vmbr9900).
The general node picker is not used because it does not prove the required no-uplink bridge exists on its
selected node. OFF is the dry
run: no PBS/PVE touch, report rendered but not sent. The scratch VMID range is RATIFIED at 9900-9999
([private detail] ruling 2) and enforced in code (band 2 refuses anything outside it) - it is not an open
confirm. Full prerequisites + first-live guided apply:
docs/dr/dr-restore-io-apply.md; design: docs/dr/weekly-dr-restore-design.md.

jobs.name: jobsearch-digest
jobs.description:
[Jobsearch] Digest

Daily email step of the Job Search Intelligence Platform (backlog 44). Renders an HTML digest
of the top matches scored above threshold in the last day (plus mailbox items needing manual
filing) and mails it to [private detail]. Each match links to its Gitea posting
file; the footer links to the Grafana dashboard.

Schedule: Daily, ~13:00 (cron('H 13 * * *')), after enrich. Agent: jobsearch. On standardPipeline, notifyOn: 'failure'.

What it does

Stage | What it does, and why

Send digest | jobsearch-send-digest.py queries postings scored >= threshold (default 60) in the last 24h with their latest gap notes, a deadline-nag section (open high-fit postings due in the next 7 days, soonest-first), a scorer-calibration section (Phase 3: outcome rate by fit-score band per prompt_ver, n≥5 floor, never pooled; hidden until data exists), plus recent Unknown (mailbox) items, renders templates/digest.html.j2, and sends it via smtplib STARTTLS with the Date + Message-ID headers amavis requires. A jobsearch-local sender, not the shared email library. Preview: Build with Parameters, DRY_RUN=true, renders digest-preview.html as a build artifact without sending.

Notification model

The sender is quiet by default - no matches and no manual items means no mail - so the
digest's arrival is the daily success heartbeat. notifyOn: 'failure'
therefore fires only when the job itself breaks (DB, Vault, or mail unreachable). A day with
matches but no email is the signal to check this job.

Prereqs: Vault secrets [private detail] and [private detail] (username, password, smtp_host, smtp_port, from); mail submission reach ([private detail]:587). Links are env-overridable (JOBSEARCH_GITEA_FILE_BASE, JOBSEARCH_DASHBOARD_URL).

jobs.name: pr-ci
jobs.description:
[CI] Pull request merge preview

Items 364/365. Builds one open automationlab pull request's merge preview and publishes a
stable jenkins/pr-ci Gitea commit status that branch protection can require. Queued only by
pr-ci-dispatch with a validated PR_NUMBER, immutable HEAD_SHA, and reviewed BASE_BRANCH -
this job never discovers PRs or holds the Gitea API token itself.

Pipeline definition, not PR content: the job is a
Job DSL Pipeline script from SCM job pinned to protected */main
(jenkins/jobs/pr_ci_jobs.groovy -> jenkins/Jenkinsfile-pr-ci). No Gitea
branch-source plugin is installed, so a same-repository PR can never select its own Jenkinsfile - only a
reviewed main commit can change what this job runs.

What it does: validates PR_NUMBER,
HEAD_SHA, and BASE_BRANCH, explicitly exports those values to shell stages, and posts a
pending status. With credential gitea-[private detail], it fetches protected
the reviewed main or develop target and refs/pull/<n>/head, proves the fetched PR head equals the requested SHA,
sets a workspace-local Jenkins committer identity, and creates the merge preview locally with
git merge --no-ff --no-edit into an ephemeral commit so history-aware checks see both parents. The test container installs the official gate's lightweight
Python dependencies and trusts only the ephemeral shared workspace for nested Git checks, then runs
scripts/run-offline-tests.py under the repository's offline suite. The run publishes and
fingerprints offline-junit.xml ([private detail]). A test or preview failure makes the build unstable
while preserving the separate completion stage, which always posts the final jenkins/pr-ci status
(success or failure) with a link back to this build.

Blank-controller readiness: Job DSL creates
all three build parameters during the seed. The first dispatcher or operator request can therefore use
buildWithParameters immediately after recovery; no failing parameterless priming build is
required.

Bounded parallelism: this runner permits
concurrent builds because every PR uses isolated ephemeral Kubernetes pods and workspaces. The serialized
dispatcher counts fresh pending reservations and admits at most four active PR heads globally, avoiding
both the former one-build backlog and unbounded pod creation.

Credential isolation: the Gitea status token
(gitea-jenkins-token) is bound only in the "Publish pending" and "Publish completion"
stages, in fresh pods that never check out PR content. The "PR merge preview" stage that runs PR-supplied
code binds no Vault AppRole and no Gitea write credential.

Apply and proof

Committed-not-applied; the guided apply/rollback procedure, including adding the required
jenkins/pr-ci context to main branch protection, is
docs/ci-cd/364-multibranch-pr-ci-apply.md.

jobs.name: zabbix-api-token-rotation
jobs.description:
Purpose: replace the read-only monitoring token and the provisioning/maintenance
token every 60 days through the supported Zabbix Token API.

The job creates 90-day replacements, validates both exact token IDs, CAS-updates the registered
Vault path, and retains seven days of overlap before deleting only the recorded predecessor. Every
daily run also validates the current provider token. The read-only cohort confirms both copied
Kubernetes Secrets still match Vault and health-checks its two consumers even when no rotation is
due. The automation cohort
has no copied value: provisioning, decommissioning, self-heal, portal, and maintenance jobs read the
canonical Vault record at invocation. Persisted phases recover interrupted activation, and token
values are never printed or exported to monitoring.

jobs.name: entra-kubernetes-credential-rotation
jobs.description:
[IAM] Kubernetes Entra SSO Credential Rotation

Daily fail-closed 60-day rotation for the Argo CD, Grafana, and Jenkins Entra confidential-client
credentials. Replacements are valid for 90 days and the exact prior key remains for a seven-day overlap.

The job updates only each registered Vault field and existing named Kubernetes Secret, then rolls only
the registered workload. Jenkins DEV is updated and verified before production. It authenticates the new
credential directly with Entra, verifies every live Secret matches Vault, and requires the workload health
and Microsoft-login routes before recording success. Failure restores Vault and every attempted consumer
while retaining both Entra credentials; secret values are never logged or passed in arguments.

jobs.name: platform-maintenance-inspect
jobs.description:
[Platform] Maintenance pilot

Daily cleanup-first assessment at 06:00 America/Denver for the enrolled Greenbone VM, plus on-demand inspection. Uses the existing provisioner and runtime Vault credentials. Only an authenticated Jenkins timer cause selects scheduled cleanup; manual runs still default to inspection.

Parameters

MODE defaults to INSPECT. CLEANUP selects one existing-policy cycle with fresh conflict checks and verified Fleet publication. A healthy disk requires no cleanup. INSTALL_RUNTIME defaults to false and is allowed only with inspection. Installation verifies the pinned bundle, safely prepares protected stores and grants exact stdio commands. Only the pinned predecessor can be upgraded atomically, retaining its complete tree; other differing or partial installations are refused.

Evidence

Inspection archives the validated observation and acceptance. Cleanup archives the cycle and acceptance bound to the exact checkout, build, result hash and independently verified receiver receipt. Requested mode, effective mode and authenticated launch cause remain distinct. No-action, deferral and partial reports are not proof of archive removal. Blocked reports fail the build and retain artifacts; unavailable publication grants no acceptance. Recovery cannot repeat deletion.

Boundary

Cleanup is limited to eligible Greenbone DNF package archives under native locks, host admission and the existing policy. No disk growth, reboot, service restart, project reservation release or migration. Conflict checks cover this operation's write set; desktop visibility is not claimed. A healthy scheduled run proves unattended assessment and reporting, not unattended repair. Do not change policy thresholds to manufacture cleanup evidence.

Runbook, credential paths and acceptance checks

jobs.name: internal-website-scan
jobs.description:
[Security] Internal website scan

Weekly anonymous checks of six internal services: Jenkins, Gitea, Grafana, Argo CD, NetBox and the fleet portal.
Exact origins, addresses, paths and response expectations are committed in security-scan/internal-website-scan.json.

Verifies internal DNS destinations, TLS trust, hostname and expiry, expected anonymous denial or SSO redirect,
cookie flags and service-specific headers. Requests are serial, one second apart, with a 64 KiB response cap.
No credentials, crawling, redirects, external research or Nuclei. Bodies and cookie values are not retained.

PROD: Saturday H 7 * * 6, private artifacts, security-store summary and sysadmin digest.
DEV: on demand, private artifacts and store preview; production database and SMTP are skipped.

Findings are advisory. Failed or incomplete checks mark the run UNSTABLE; an anonymous scan is not
authenticated application coverage. Runbook: docs/pipelines/internal-website-scan.md.

Managed in git: jenkins/Jenkinsfile-internal-website-scan.

jobs.name: backup-digest
jobs.description:
[Ops] Backup Digest

Daily brand-styled digest of Proxmox Backup Server status so backup health is visible without
logging into PBS. It exists because of a week-long silent backup failure (June 2026, a stale
iSCSI portal IP) that went unseen because the only alert went to unread local mail. Now every
morning a showpiece lands in [private detail]: an orientation intro, a stale
headline, two inline charts (backup freshness + DR coverage), and a per-guest 7-day history per
datastore, with failures and stale rows in red. Deleted-guest snapshots are separated out so they
never false-alarm ([private detail]), and a genuine staleness or failure among existing guests fires
a dedicated [ALERT] email to the alert group ([private detail]).

Schedule: Daily, ~07:00 (cron('H 7 * * *')), after the 01:30 backup window. Agent: provisioner. On standardPipeline, notifyOn: 'failure'.

What it does

Stage | What it does, and why

Backup digest | pbs-backup-digest.py reads the PBS API (snapshots + task history, no scraping) for nas-datastore and dr-datastore, maps VMIDs to guest names via the PVE API (fail-soft to type/vmid), and renders a brand-palette showpiece: intro, stale headline, two inline HTML/CSS charts (backup freshness + DR coverage gap), and a per-guest 7-day history per datastore. Sent via the shared labmail.py (Vault creds + verified TLS). PBS token from Vault [private detail] guest names from [private detail] Existing-vs-deleted classification via the live PVE guest list moves deleted-guest snapshots to a separate "Retained snapshots" section ([private detail], with reclaimable space); a genuine staleness/failure among existing guests raises a dedicated [ALERT] email ([private detail]). Failures and stale rows are red; a trend chart is deferred (see runbook).

Notification model

Three signals. (1) The digest email arrives daily to [private detail] - its
arrival means the job ran. (2) A genuine staleness/failure among existing guests sends a
dedicated [ALERT] Backup staleness email to [private detail] ([private detail]):
any failed backup, or 3+ stale guests, or a guest stale beyond 2 days (env-overridable); deleted-guest
ghosts ([private detail]) never trigger it. (3) notifyOn: 'failure' fires only when the digest job
itself fails (PBS/Vault/mail unreachable). The exit code stays honest - alerting on staleness is the
email, not a failed build, so "backups are stale" stays distinct from "the digest broke". Remaining gap:
a digest that never runs at all (dead-man's-switch) is a noted future follow-up.

Rendering

The showpiece HTML is built in the collector (bespoke brand palette + inline HTML/CSS charts);
only the send path is shared (labmail.send_html: Vault-sourced SMTP creds,
verified TLS). labmail's generic section renderer (render_report) stays
available for plainer future reports, e.g. a nightly database pg_dump summary. The
failures/stale trend chart is deferred (a CSS time series is not clean and history is thin).

Prereqs: read-only PBS API token in Vault [private detail] (creation steps in docs/backlog/17-backup-digest-email.md); PVE creds [private detail] for guest names (fail-soft); Jinja2 on the provisioner image (via ansible-core); TLS trust for the mail submission cert (LAB_CA_BUNDLE), the PBS API cert, and the PVE API cert (PROXMOX_TLS_INSECURE=1 matches the other PVE tooling).

jobs.name: estate-drift-assurance
jobs.description:
[Assurance] Estate-wide Drift and Source Assurance

Weekly, read-only reconciliation across the estate's record, configuration, and infrastructure state.

Surface | Evidence

Sources of truth | Compares active Ansible inventory, HostManifests, NetBox devices/VMs/named IPs, live Proxmox guests, and Zabbix hosts. It reports membership, IP, VMID, and placement divergence without writing any API.

Ansible configuration | Runs the committed Linux baseline/NTP and scoped firewall plays with --check --diff. Findings name host, role, task, and a bounded redacted diff. Secret-dependent surfaces are explicit coverage exclusions.

Terraform state | Plans every backend workspace from committed configuration and HostManifest inputs. Non-empty plans are drift; remotely deleted resources are labeled state orphans for an operator-gated re-import or state rm decision.

Results: SUCCESS is a measured clean baseline, UNSTABLE is advisory drift, and FAILURE means at least one surface was unreadable. Markdown and JSON reports are archived on every run. There is no remediation, apply, destroy, import, or state mutation stage.

jobs.name: cityamble-app-release-aab
jobs.description:
[CityAmble] Android release AAB

Manually builds and verifies a signed Android App Bundle for the CityAmble Play upload. Requires a clean checkout whose commit equals fetched protected origin/main, even when the checkout wrapper leaves branch metadata blank. Runs on the dedicated Android build agent and reads the upload key only from Vault through the narrowly scoped cityamble-android-signing-ro credential.

jobs.name: aiops-triage
jobs.description:
[AIOps] Morning Triage

The daily AIOps morning-triage chain ([private detail]). One job runs the whole loop before the
operator sits down: collect the last 24h of events from four sources, triage each
finding (classify, correlate, rationale), and email one grouped digest to
[private detail]. Read-only end to end: no actions, no PR generation
(Phase 5 is hard-gated). Local-first inference classifies; hard cases use the same usage-aware
headless router as job scoring. It reads the hourly subscription observation, chooses Codex or
Claude only when safe headroom remains, and fails closed without a metered model API.

Schedule: Daily, ~06:00 (cron('H 6 * * *')), after the 01:30 backups and before the 07:00 backup digest. Agent: jobsearch. On standardPipeline, notifyOn: 'failure'.

What it does

Stage | What it does, and why

Collect x4 | collect-alertmanager / -zabbix / -jenkins / -backup .py pull the last 24h into the normalized findings table. Each is wrapped catchError -> UNSTABLE: one dead source marks the build unstable but the chain continues, and the failure is recorded so the digest can name it.

Triage | triage-findings.py classifies each finding (known-noise / needs-info / actionable), groups by host correlation, and consults the signature history. Also catchError -> UNSTABLE: if the Ollama box is off, triage exits non-zero and records a triage-engine finding, and the digest reports "triage did not run" instead of green-empty.

Digest | send-digest.py renders one grouped email: actionable (with the triage rationale), needs-info (each carrying the exact diagnostic command, host named), and known-noise suppressed (each with its history citation, e.g. "seen 3x, ruled noise, last 07-12"). Sent via aiops_notify.py (hvac creds + labmail's verified TLS, no vault CLI). Not wrapped: a render/DB/mail failure fails the build.

Notification model (dead-man's-switch)

The digest email is the daily success signal (backup-digest pattern). Graduated failure per [private detail]'s lesson: a single dead source or the Ollama box being off still produces a digest that
says so in a red DEGRADED banner (collectors/triage stale) - never a green
empty email. Only the digest itself failing (DB or mail unreachable) fails the build, at
which point notifyOn: 'failure' pages and no email arrives - that absence is
the alert. A digest_runs heartbeat row is written every real send so "did the digest
run today" is queryable.

Preview

Build with Parameters -> DRY_RUN = true renders aiops-digest-preview.html
from existing DB data as a build artifact, collecting/triaging/sending nothing. Also runnable on
the agent: py -3 aiops/scripts/send-digest.py --dry-run.

Prereqs: the Phase 1/2 bootstrap (aiops DB + role, Vault [private detail] [private detail] reused zabbix/pbs/proxmox secrets); migrations applied through 003_digest.sql; the AppRole granted read on [private detail] and fresh hourly subscription-usage metrics. Agent deps include hvac, psycopg2, requests, Jinja2, and the Codex and Claude CLIs.

jobs.description:
[IAM] Proxmox and PBS API Token Rotation

Automatically replaces the registered read-only PVE exporter and PBS digest API tokens every 60 days.

The replacement expires after 90 days. A forced-command SSH identity can invoke only an allowlisted host helper. The helper copies the predecessor privilege mode and exact ACL rows, returns the one-time value without logging it, and permits deletion only inside the registered provider identity.

jobs.name: zabbix-psk-rotation
jobs.description:
Zabbix Linux agent PSK rotation.

Daily 60-day evaluation of proved Linux PSKs, plus an explicit forced path for a pending canary. The job verifies Vault and authenticated host fingerprints, changes the agent and exact Zabbix host, requires a fresh passive check, and commits Vault last. Any failed validation restores the previous PSK on both sides.

jobs.name: provision-windows
jobs.description:
AutomationLab - Self-Service Windows VM Provisioning

Parameterised, self-service pipeline that provisions a fully network-configured, monitored,
domain-joined Windows Server VM on the Proxmox cluster. The operator picks the
Windows Server version (2022 or 2025), CPU/RAM, storage class, OS disk size, an
optional second data disk, and optional tools/features. The pipeline resolves the right
template by tag, allocates an IP from NetBox, selects a hypervisor by live
resource availability, clones the template, gates the apply behind a human
approval, configures the host with Ansible over WinRM/HTTPS, registers it in
Zabbix, joins it to Active Directory, enforces Duo MFA on RDP logins,
creates its DNS records, and commits a host manifest to git so a re-run against
the same host is a safe reconcile (node reused, no destroy) rather than a rebuild.

Templates (resolved by tag, not hardcoded ID)

Templates are tagged in Proxmox and resolved at runtime, so a rebuilt template can take any
free VM ID - no renumbering, no Terraform edits. Provisioned VMs do not keep
inherited template tags: the pipeline clears them post-apply via the Proxmox API
(clear-tags.py), so only real templates carry
win-template/os-*. Templates ship with a 24 GB OS
disk; the pipeline expands to the selected size on every build.

OS | Proxmox tags | Current VMID / node

Windows Server 2022 | win-template, os-2022 | 892 / pve2

Windows Server 2025 | win-template, os-2025 | 9025 / proxmox

What it does (stage by stage)

Validate input - NetBIOS-safe VM_NAME (≤15 chars),
rejects any expected parameter that arrives empty (ROLE,
CORES, MEMORY_GB, TEMPLATE_OS, STORAGE,
DISK_GB, DATA_DISK_GB) or that carries an
ERROR_LOADING_* Active Choices fallback sentinel, computes memory in MB, and
validates disk sizes against storage capacity (NVMe ≤ 400 GB/disk, NFS ≤
2000 GB).

Checkout - checkout scm; brings in Terraform, scripts,
playbooks, and any existing host_vars/<name>.yml manifest on main
(which drives replay mode below).

Allocate IP from NetBox - reserves the next free address in the role's
prefix; the bare IP yields a collision-free Proxmox VM ID and the gateway.

Select Node - ranks online nodes by free memory, runs a disk pre-flight
sized to the requested disk. Replay-aware ([private detail]): if a manifest with a
recorded node already exists, that node is reused and node ranking is skipped, so a
re-run against an existing host never makes Terraform plan a destroy+recreate.

Generate local-admin password - AppRole login to Vault, per-host
Administrator password stored at [private detail]<host>.

Resolve Template - resolve-template.py os-<TEMPLATE_OS>
returns the tagged template's VMID and node.

Terraform Plan - per-VM workspace, is_windows=true, with the
resolved template id/node passed in.

Approval - HTML e-mail to [private detail] with VM
details and a deep link; manual Apply / Abort gate with a 60-minute timeout ([private detail]; no response aborts and rolls forward, IP released). If the plan forces a
replacement of an existing host ([private detail]), the subject and banner turn red
DESTRUCTIVE and the button becomes DESTROY & RECREATE -
so a re-run can never silently rebuild a live VM.

Terraform Apply - full-clones the resolved template to the chosen node,
applies the cloud-init drive (static IP, gateway, DNS), and boots; then clears the
clone-inherited template tags via the Proxmox API.

Register Zabbix - per-host PSK, Zabbix host against the Windows group and
template.

Wait for WinRM - polls 5986 until the first-boot LocalScript has stood up
the listener and set the bootstrap password.

Expand OS disk (when DISK_GB > 24 -
effectively always, since the smallest selection is 40 and templates are 24 GB)
- grows the OS disk via the Proxmox API (no-op if already at target); the guest
extend happens in Ansible.

Move disk to NVMe (when STORAGE=NVMe) -
online migration to node-local-lvm, transparent to the guest.

Add data disk (when DATA_DISK_GB ≠ None)
- attaches a new disk on the OS disk's storage; guest init/format in Ansible.

Configure (Ansible) - rotate password → expand C: → rename +
domain-join (Servers OU) → Zabbix agent → time → firewall →
Duo MFA (credential provider, RDP-only prompt, fail-open when offline, keys
from Vault) → tools → features → data disk. All secrets from Vault.

DNS Register (windows agent) -
Register-DnsRecord.ps1 creates the [private detail] A record
on the DC, then the reverse PTR only if the subnet's /24 reverse zone exists
(queried, not assumed); it reports A and PTR separately and skips the PTR with an
explicit message when the zone is missing ([private detail] - no more silent "A + PTR"
hiding a WIN32 9715). Plus [private detail] when PUBLISH_DNS is set.

Write host manifest - last stage: reaching it means the whole provision
succeeded. write-host-manifest.py then gitCommitPush opens a
jenkins-bot PR for inventory/host_vars/<name>.yml (flavor, template OS,
node, tools/features) and blocks until it is durably merged. Provision does not report
success until the manifest is automatically merged on main ([private detail]).

Notify / Cleanup - e-mails success; on failure, conditionally releases the
NetBox IP (retained once the VM exists, so a re-run rolls forward); a failed release logs a WARN and marks the build UNSTABLE ([private detail] finding 2, no longer || true).

Parameters

Parameter | Description

VM_NAME | Hostname (no domain). Max 15 chars (NetBIOS). Becomes the computer name and Terraform workspace name.

ROLE | VLAN/prefix the IP is drawn from (infra/control/ci → .10, kubernetes → .20, identity → .30, clients → .40).

CORES | vCPU count - 4 / 6 / 8.

MEMORY_GB | RAM in GB - 4 / 6 / 8 / 10 / 12.

TEMPLATE_OS | Windows Server version - 2022 or 2025 (resolves the tagged template).

STORAGE | NFS (shared) or NVMe (node-local, faster).

DISK_GB | OS disk size (reactive: NVMe ≤ 400, NFS ≤ 2000). Templates are 24 GB, so every selection (40 minimum) triggers an expand.

DATA_DISK_GB | Optional second data disk (reactive, same caps). None = no second disk.

PUBLISH_DNS | Also create a [private detail] record. Default false.

TOOLS | Multi-select: user tools via Chocolatey.

FEATURES | Multi-select: Windows roles/features, install-only.

All parameters are defined in the Jenkinsfile via properties([parameters([...])]).
DISK_GB/DATA_DISK_GB are reactive (Active Choices) and narrow their
options based on STORAGE. New params appear in the form after the first run
registers them. Because this is properties() and not a declarative
parameters {} block, a non-UI trigger can leave a parameter unset, so
Validate input fails fast on an empty one instead of defaulting.

Disk handling

OS disk grows cleanly - both templates are laid out with C: as the last
partition (WinRE inside C:), so resize + Resize-Partition just works.
Templates are 24 GB, so the expand stage fires on every build.

Second disk - attached on the OS disk's storage, initialised by Ansible,
lands on the next free letter (usually E:, since D: is the cloud-init CD-ROM).

Capacity guard - NVMe capped at 400 GB/disk, NFS at 2000 GB, enforced in
both the dropdowns and the Validate stage.

MFA (Duo)

Every provisioned VM gets the Duo Windows Logon credential provider via the
duo-winlogon role: silent exe install, RDP-only prompting (Proxmox
console logins are never blocked), fail-open when Duo is unreachable, install
verified by checking the credential provider DLL. Integration keys live in Vault at
[private detail] Access is scoped to the lab-admins Duo group.

Bootstrap, hostname & password rotation

The template ships a bootstrap Administrator password and a cloudbase-init LocalScript that,
on first boot, sets the password, stands up WinRM-HTTPS, and opens the firewall. The first
Ansible role rotates the password to a per-host Vault value. Because Proxmox's configdrive2
carries no hostname, the computer is renamed by Ansible before the domain join. DNS
records are created authoritatively on a domain-joined windows agent. On
decommission, the per-host local-admin password is retained in Vault so a VM restored
from PBS backup remains loginable.

Runs on

The provisioner Kubernetes pod agent (ephemeral; Ansible Windows collections
installed at runtime). DNS stage on a windows agent. Builds from
main (Gitea admin/automationlab,
jenkins/Jenkinsfile-provision-windows).

Dev guardrail (ADR-0018): on the dev controller (CONTROLLER_ENV=dev) Terraform Apply is skipped (plan-only); set APPLY_ON_DEV=true to provision for real. Prod provisions as normal.

Operator runbook: docs/pipelines/provision-windows.md.
Full architecture and prerequisites:
automationlab/docs/provisioning/provisioning-pipeline-windows.md.

jobs.name: decommission-linux
jobs.description:
[VM] Decommission Linux

The reverse of the Linux provision pipeline: it permanently destroys a VM and undoes every side
effect provisioning created - the Terraform-built VM, the NetBox IP reservation, the Zabbix
host, the DNS records, and the committed host manifest - behind a human approval. It exists
so a retired VM leaves nothing orphaned: no ghost IP, no stale monitoring host that pages forever,
no dangling DNS, no abandoned Terraform state. A single VM_NAME drives the whole
teardown, keyed to the per-VM Terraform workspace.

Schedule: On demand (Build with Parameters). Agent: provisioner pod for everything except DNS Deregister, which hops to a windows agent.

What it does (stage by stage)

Stage | What it does, and why

Validate input | Trims/validates VM_NAME. The name selects the workspace that will be destroyed, so this fails fast on a bad value.

Terraform Plan (destroy) | Selects the workspace, reads the real IP via terraform output -raw vm_ip (captured for the later IP/PTR release), and stages a saved -destroy plan. It also drops the shared cached Rocky image from state so destroy never deletes the shared datastore file.

Approval | Red HTML email to [private detail], then a manual gate: PERMANENTLY DESTROY <name> (<ip>)?, button Destroy. The gate has a 30-minute timeout ([private detail]): no response aborts before anything is destroyed.

Remove host manifest (runs before destroy) | gitCommitPush(remove:true) opens a jenkins-bot PR for inventory/host_vars/<name>.yml and blocks until it is durably auto-merged on main. The VMID/IP cannot be reused until the manifest is off main. A missing manifest is a no-op. If the merge fails, the stage fails and no VM is destroyed.

Terraform Destroy | Applies the exact approved destroy plan - the VM is gone after this. The manifest has already been durably removed before this stage runs.

Release IP from NetBox (if IP recovered) | netbox-release-ip.py <ip> returns the address to the pool. Skipped if the plan stage could not recover a valid IP.

Deregister Zabbix | zabbix-delete-host.py <name> (token from [private detail] removes the monitoring host so it stops alerting.

DNS Deregister (windows agent) | Idempotent removal on the DC: A records for the host in [private detail] and [private detail], plus the reverse PTR when a valid IP is known. (Linux VMs are not domain-joined, so there is no AD computer object to remove - DNS only.)

Delete workspace | Selects default then deletes the now-empty per-VM Terraform workspace.

Parameters

Param | Meaning, default, consequence

VM_NAME | Hostname / Terraform workspace to destroy. Regex-validated. This single value keys the entire teardown, so a wrong name destroys the wrong workspace.

Failure & rollback

post success: emails "VM Decommissioned" to [private detail].
post failure: emails "VM Decommission FAILED" with the build URL. There is no automated
rollback (nothing to undo on a teardown); re-run to complete a partial decommission - each
stage is safe to repeat.

Note: Destructive and irreversible - verify VM_NAME before approving. IP release and PTR removal depend on recovering a valid IP from Terraform output; if that is missing they are silently skipped (possible orphaned IP). The windows agent must be online for DNS Deregister.

Dev guardrail (ADR-0018): on the dev controller (CONTROLLER_ENV=dev) Terraform Destroy, Release IP from NetBox, Deregister Zabbix, and DNS Deregister are all skipped (plan-only); set APPLY_ON_DEV=true to run them for real. Prod runs every stage as normal.

Reads [private detail] (username/password) and [private detail] from Vault at runtime (ADR-0010); no credential on the command line. The manager serves a self-signed cert, so verification is off by default (WAZUH_API_INSECURE=1) until a trusted cert is in place.

jobs.name: cleanup-disabled-users
jobs.description:
[IAM] Sweep Disabled Users

The deletion half of disable-first offboarding, and a daily audit of the Disabled OU. Deprovision
deliberately only disables a user; this job permanently deletes accounts that have sat
disabled longer than the grace period, so the OU does not accumulate stale objects forever. Just as
importantly, it surfaces anomalies - an enabled account sitting in the Disabled OU, or a
disabled account with no offboard record - that indicate someone bypassed the pipeline. It
enforces retention policy automatically while flagging drift for a human.

Schedule: Daily, ~06:00 (cron('H 6 * * *')). Also runnable on demand. Agent: agent none, stages hop provisioner/windows. No approval gate.

What it does (stage by stage)

Stage | What it does, and why

Wrap vault token (provisioner) | AppRole-logs in and captures a short-lived Vault token for the Windows stage, which needs to read offboard dates from Vault. (Unlike the other IAM pipelines this passes a plain token, not a response-wrapped one - a broader exposure.)

Sweep (windows) | Sweep-DisabledUsers.ps1 enumerates [private detail]

Notify (provisioner) | sweep-notify.py parses the report and emails [private detail] (SMTP creds from Vault [private detail] only when there were deletions or anomalies - unless ALWAYS_EMAIL. Keeps quiet days silent so the report stays signal, not noise; subject gains [ANOMALIES] when relevant.

Parameters

Param | Meaning, default, consequence

GRACE_DAYS | Default 30. Delete accounts disabled at least this many days. Lower = accounts deleted sooner - the safety window before permanent deletion.

ALWAYS_EMAIL | Default false. When false, email is sent only on deletions/anomalies; when true, sent even on a "waiting only" day. Controls daily confirmation vs. report noise.

Failure & behavior

No post block - reporting is the notify stage, not a post handler. Deletion is
irreversible and has no undo. A failed run shows as a red build; the next daily run continues
where policy dictates. Deletion depends on the Vault offboard record's disabled_date;
accounts without a record are never deleted, only flagged.

Note: Destructive and automatic - it PERMANENTLY deletes AD accounts past the grace threshold on a daily cron with no approval gate. An enabled account in the Disabled OU is flagged and skipped (never deleted). With ALWAYS_EMAIL=false a clean day produces no email, so absence of email is not proof the job ran. Notify recipient is [private detail] (not yet on the platform@ group).

Source: iam/Jenkinsfile-sweep | Managed in git - edit the file, not this box.

jobs.name: upgrade-prometheus
jobs.description:
[Platform] Upgrade Prometheus

Executable, auditable upgrade / re-apply of the kube-prometheus-stack Helm release
(prometheus in namespace monitoring) from the values file tracked in git
(k8s/monitoring/prometheus-values.yaml). It replaces the manual
helm upgrade that was run by hand, wrapping it in a diff preview, a manual approval
gate, and a post-upgrade rollout check. [private detail] / [private detail].

Run mode: On demand (NOT scheduled). Unlike
Upgrade Jenkins (weekly cron auto-reapply), this job gates the upgrade behind manual approval,
so an unattended schedule would only stall at the gate. Agent: an inline Kubernetes pod with a standard
jnlp (jenkins/inbound-agent) plus an alpine/k8s helm container
carrying the jenkins-helm service account; all cluster work runs in container('helm')
(the ADR-0006 in-cluster, unprivileged, scoped-ServiceAccount posture).

What it does (stage by stage)

Stage | What it does, and why

Verify values present | Confirms k8s/monitoring/prometheus-values.yaml exists in the automationlab checkout ([private detail] source of truth), failing clearly rather than applying an empty/default release.

Preview (diff / plan) | Adds the prometheus-community repo, then shows what the upgrade would change before anything is applied. Uses helm diff upgrade if the helm-diff plugin is present; otherwise falls back to helm template (proposed) vs helm get manifest (live) as a unified diff (indicative, not exact).

Approve upgrade | Manual input gate after the preview, with a 60-minute timeout (an abandoned build aborts rather than waiting forever). Nothing has changed in the cluster up to this point.

Helm upgrade | helm upgrade prometheus prometheus-community/kube-prometheus-stack -n monitoring --version <CHART_VERSION> -f k8s/monitoring/prometheus-values.yaml. Explicit --version pin means the chart never moves on its own.

Post-upgrade rollout check | kubectl -n monitoring rollout status deploy/prometheus-grafana --timeout=300s plus helm status. A stuck rollout fails the build, so a broken upgrade is loud.

Parameters

CHART_VERSION - kube-prometheus-stack chart version to apply. Defaults to 86.0.2 (the pinned, in-use chart); re-running with the default re-asserts the committed values. Bumping it is a real upgrade - review the preview carefully.

Failure & behavior

On every run the standard labNotify mails [private detail] with
subject [<result>] <job> #<n> (the shared standardPipeline helper).
No rollback: a failed helm upgrade leaves the previous revision running (Helm keeps
history) - investigate and re-run, or helm rollback prometheus <rev> -n monitoring to
revert deliberately. Concurrent builds are disabled so two upgrades cannot race.

Prerequisites (the job does not create these): (1) RBAC - jenkins-helm is scoped to the jenkins namespace today; a helm-release-manager Role + RoleBinding must be added in monitoring (binding SA jenkins/jenkins-helm) before the first run. (2) The monitoring/grafana-jobsearch-pg secret must exist ([private detail]; run scripts/create-grafana-jobsearch-pg-secret.sh). (3) helm-diff is optional. Full detail and the RBAC manifest: docs/ci-cd/upgrade-prometheus.md.
