jobs.name: deprovision-user
jobs.description:
[IAM] Deprovision User

Disable-first offboarding across AD, Entra, file shares, and mail in one controlled run. Rather
than deleting an account outright (which loses the mailbox, home data, and any chance of an
"oops, wrong person" recovery), it disables the account, moves it to [private detail]
strips group access, and hands the home folder and mailbox to the manager - then records the
offboard date in Vault so the daily sweep can permanently delete it after a grace period. It exists
to make offboarding reversible-until-grace and to guarantee the departed user's data and mail are
preserved for whoever inherits them.

Schedule: On demand, behind two gates: a CONFIRM checkbox interlock and a four-eyes approval (a second person must approve; the approver cannot be the requester). Agent: agent none, stages hop windows/provisioner. The NAS service-account credential crosses to Windows only as a single-use wrapped token.

What it does (stage by stage)

Stage | What it does, and why

Gate | Errors out unless CONFIRM is ticked and SAM is non-empty - a hard interlock against an accidental or empty offboard. Also captures the requesting user from the build cause for the four-eyes check.

Lookup target (windows, read-only) | Get-ADUser reads the target's display name, department, and manager so the approver sees who they are offboarding. Non-destructive, and fails fast if the SAM does not exist - it runs before anything is changed.

Four-eyes approval (agent none) | Emails DL-SysAdmin ([private detail]) with the target context (SAM, display name, department, manager), the requester, and a direct link to the input. A second person approves via the Jenkins input step; the approver's identity is captured and must differ from the requester (segregation of duties) or the build hard-fails. A 24h timeout aborts a stuck request. Runs before the wrapped credential is minted and before any destructive stage.

Snapshot offboard state (provisioner, [private detail]) | Records the pre-strip AD state (groups, UPN, OU, manager, enabled) captured read-only in Lookup to offboarded/<sam>-<date>.yml and commits it to main as jenkins-bot (write-offboard-snapshot.py + gitCommitPush, [skip ci]). Runs after approval but before any strip, so the exact restore source exists before anything changes. Idempotent (skips if a snapshot already exists for the SAM). This is what makes a wrongly-offboarded or swept user a clean restore rather than an approximation.

Wrap homemove credential (provisioner) | Mints a 15-minute single-use wrapped token carrying the [private detail] NAS credential (Vault [private detail] so the Windows stage gets privileged NAS access without the password appearing in plaintext.

AD deprovision (windows) | Remove-LabUser.ps1: refuses if the user is outside the managed OU; resolves the manager from AD; disables and datestamps the account; removes all groups (keeps Domain Users); moves it to [private detail]

Entra scrub (provisioner) | entra-deprovision.py removes the user from all cloud groups and app-role assignments (tiles disappear), and writes the offboard record to Vault [private detail]<sam> (disabled_date, manager, status) - the record the sweep depends on. A 404 in Entra exits 0 (already gone).

Mail handoff (provisioner) | If a manager was resolved: over SSH to the mail VM, imports the departed maildir into the manager's mailbox as Departed.<sam> (idempotent), subscribes the manager, and installs a sieve vacation auto-reply pointing senders at the manager. Skipped entirely if no manager.

Parameters

Param | Meaning, default, consequence

SAM | sAMAccountName of the user to offboard. Drives the UPN and every downstream lookup.

CONFIRM | Default false. Safety interlock - if not ticked the build errors immediately. Prevents accidental destructive offboarding.

Failure & rollback

A pending offboard emails DL-SysAdmin for approval (see the four-eyes stage); a
rejected, same-person, or timed-out approval fails or aborts the build before any change is made.
On completion there is a post success echo summary (manager received H:\Departed-<SAM>
and mailbox Departed.<SAM>; account disabled in [private detail]
separate sweep). There is no automated rollback. Recovery from a mid-run failure is re-run
(idempotent). Wrong-user recovery while still within the grace period: re-enable the account, move it
back out of [private detail]

Four-eyes limitation (honest): this is a single-operator lab, so in practice both the requester and the approver are the same person (Bill). The control demonstrates the enterprise segregation-of-duties pattern and is enforced literally - a same-person approval hard-fails. It must not block solo operation: the escape is the built-in 24h timeout-then-abort (do nothing and let it lapse), or approving from a genuinely separate admin account. The gate is real, not cosmetic; the workaround is documented rather than the check being weakened.

Note: The account is NOT deleted here - deletion is the sweep's job after the grace period, so this stays reversible until then. Home/mail handoff has silent skip/warn edges: no home folder = skip; a home folder but no manager (or a manager with no home) = warn and leave the data in place. If no manager resolves, the mail handoff is skipped and the offboard record stores an empty manager. The wrapped homemove token is single-use / 15-min TTL.

Source: iam/Jenkinsfile-deprovision-user | Managed in git - edit the file, not this box.

jobs.name: vault-approle-secret-rotation
jobs.description:
[IAM] Jenkins Vault AppRole SecretID Rotation

Daily fail-closed 60-day rotation for the long-lived Jenkins Vault AppRole SecretID and the narrowly scoped rotation AppRole's own bootstrap SecretID.

For each due registered target, the job mints a 90-day replacement, CAS-updates only its exact custody record, patches only its existing named Kubernetes Secret, waits for the projected value, and authenticates to Vault as that AppRole. The old SecretID remains valid for seven days and is destroyed only by its exact accessor after revalidation. Failures restore Vault and Kubernetes while retaining both SecretIDs for recovery.

jobs.name: zabbix-maintenance
jobs.description:
[Ops] Zabbix Maintenance Windows

Creates Zabbix maintenance windows on demand so planned work - patching, reboots, a
disruptive change, a provision run - does not page anyone or bury the real signal under
self-inflicted alerts. Without it an operator either silences monitoring by hand (and forgets
to turn it back on) or accepts an alert storm during every planned change. The job takes a
host list, a duration, and a start time, and creates a one-shot maintenance window per host
via the Zabbix API. It is the front half of a pair: the daily cleanup job removes the expired
window objects this one leaves behind.

Schedule: On demand (Build with Parameters). No trigger - an operator runs it before planned work. Agent: a Kubernetes pod on the zabbix-agent image (ships zabbix_utils + pytz).

What it does (stage by stage)

Stage | What it does, and why

Enable Maintenance | Logs in to the Zabbix API ([private detail] with an api_token pulled from Vault [private detail] - never a stored credential. Resolves the start time (rejecting anything in the past, so a typo cannot create a useless window), then for each host creates a one-time window named Jenkins-maintenance-<host>-<epoch>. The name prefix is deliberate: it is how the cleanup job later recognizes windows it is allowed to delete. Unknown host names are logged and skipped rather than failing the whole batch, so one bad name does not block the rest.

Parameters

Param | Meaning, default, consequence

HOST_NAME | Comma-separated list of Zabbix host display names (not IPs). Each gets its own window. A name Zabbix does not know is skipped with a log line - check the console if a host keeps alerting.

DURATION_MINUTES | Window length in minutes. Sets both the maintenance period and its end time; when it elapses the window stops suppressing on its own - no need to close it manually.

START_TIME | NOW for immediate, or YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM in America/Denver. A past time or a bad format exits non-zero and fails the build, so you cannot create a window that is already over.

Failure & behavior

No rollback: creating a maintenance window is additive and self-expiring, so a failed run
leaves nothing to undo. A past START_TIME or invalid format fails the build before
any window is created. If the Zabbix API is unreachable the login fails and the build errors;
re-run once it is back. On failure the standard labNotify mails
[private detail] (notifyOn: 'failure', added when the job moved
onto the standardPipeline shared library - previously it had none); no approval gate.

Note: Suppression, not silence - problems still record against the host, alerts just do not fire during the window. Windows expire on their own; the zabbix-cleanup-expired-maintenance job removes the husks daily. An unknown host name is silently skipped, so verify the console output if a host keeps paging.

jobs.name: sync-public-site
jobs.description:
[Publish] Sync site to public GitHub

Mirrors the reviewed site/ content from this private repo to the PUBLIC GitHub repo
billgernert/billgernert-site when a merge to main touches site/**.
A fail-closed scrub gate runs over the exact publish set before any push, so internal
content can never reach the public repo by accident. [private detail]; automates the manual
site-public/ copy from [private detail].

Trigger: a Gitea push webhook on this repo (one-time operator setup) plus an in-pipeline diff filter on site/** and docs/backlog/README.md (the latter is the item-94 roadmap-currency trigger) - NOT cron. Agent: provisioner. On standardPipeline, notifyOn: 'failure'.

What it does

Stage | What it does, and why

Detect site/ change | git diff HEAD^1 HEAD -- site/ docs/backlog/README.md; a push that touches neither is a clean no-op. The docs/backlog/README.md path ([private detail]) republishes on a backlog-only done-flip so the generated roadmap block refreshes. A missing parent (shallow checkout) proceeds - the sync is idempotent.

Stage publish set | Maps site/index.html + site/_headers to the repo root, site/capabilities/ to capabilities/, site/roadmap/ to roadmap/, site/ai/ to ai/, site/projects/ to projects/, site/platform/ to platform/, and site/diagram/ to diagram/ (a PUBLIC rendition; the internal docs/architecture/automationlab-diagram.html carries addresses and is never staged), plus every per-topic page directory in the Jenkinsfile's explicit cp list (writeups/, operations/, security/, claude-code/ and the rest) and SANITIZATION.md. A new page directory must be added to all three lists (stage cp, mirror cp, git add) or it stages and never publishes; scripts/check-site-sync-mapping.py is the CI guard for that. Then it drops PUBLISHING-CHECKLIST.md (internal; it contains the very patterns the gate greps for). Then the item-94 roadmap sub-step runs gen-roadmap-data.py --in-place to inject generated tier tallies, an "as of" date, and the curated recently-delivered list into the staged roadmap page - before the scrub, so the generated block is scrubbed like everything else. Allowlist-grade: only integers, an ISO date, fixed tier names, and verbatim Public: one-liners of done items; never a raw title; fail-closed on any internal string. The same call also refreshes the item-136 hero facts in the staged index.html (--hero-page): the delivered-item count into HERO:ITEMS, and gen-pr-count.py writes the merged-PR count into HERO:PRS (Gitea merged-PR API when a read-only GITEA_PR_TOKEN is present, else a git merge-commit fallback). Integers only.

Scrub gate (fail-closed) | Greps the staged files for internal IPs, [private detail], internal hostnames ([private detail], [private detail], DCs), the Vault port [private detail], private-key markers, and [private detail] fingerprints. Any hit fails the build and nothing is pushed. It logs path:line: [category] match masked (N chars) - the matched text is never printed, only its category and length, so the log leaks nothing.

Publish to GitHub | Clones the public repo, replaces index.html/_headers and mirrors capabilities/, roadmap/, ai/, projects/, platform/, diagram/ and every per-topic page directory in the mapping, including writeups/ and operations/ (all with deletion), leaving the public README.md/LICENSE/DEPLOY.md and its own .github/ (item-77 site-ci, hand-committed there) untouched. Commit is scope-first (site: publish from automationlab@<sha>). Idempotent no-op if already in sync. On an actual push it writes a .published marker in the workspace, which is the only thing that triggers the purge stage.

Purge Cloudflare cache | Purges the Cloudflare edge cache for [private detail] and [private detail] so that "published" means "visible" (on 2026-08-09 a publish succeeded and the pages stayed stale until a hand purge). The managed token comes from Vault at runtime and is replaced by the Cloudflare credential lifecycle every 60 days. It carries only Zone Read and Cache Purge on the two registered zones. Skipped when the publish pushed nothing. FAIL SOFT: the publish has already landed by then, so any failure marks this stage UNSTABLE, leaves the build SUCCESS, and points to the lifecycle job. If the purge does not run, the page can remain stale until Cloudflare refreshes it.

GitHub auth

The fine-grained PAT at Vault [private detail] (field token) is read via withLabVault at runtime and used through an HTTP Basic http.extraHeader, so it never lands in a remote URL, in persisted git config, or in the build log.

Prereqs: the Vault PAT above (Contents: write on billgernert/billgernert-site); this Pipeline-from-SCM job pointed at jenkins/Jenkinsfile-sync-public-site; the Gitea push build trigger enabled on the job; a Gitea push webhook on this repo; and the committed Cloudflare credential bootstrap completed once. See the runbook.

jobs.name: jobsearch-db-backup
jobs.description:
[Jobsearch] DB Backup

Nightly pg_dump of both the jobsearch and selfheal
databases on the in-cluster Postgres, gzipped and pushed to the Synology NAS with ~14-day
retention. A Phase 1 deliverable (backlog 44) that also closes the pre-existing gap that the
self-heal DB was never backed up - which is why it covers selfheal too, not
just jobsearch.

Schedule: Nightly, ~02:00 (cron('H 2 * * *')). Agent: jobsearch (image carries postgresql-client + smbclient). On standardPipeline, notifyOn: 'failure'.

What it does

Stage | What it does, and why

Backup databases | jobsearch-db-backup.py runs pg_dump | gzip for each DB to <db>-YYYYMMDD-HHMMSS.sql.gz, uploads over SMB to the NAS, then prunes remote dumps older than 14 days (by the date in the filename; only files matching the dump pattern are ever deleted). Notification model

notifyOn: 'failure' is the entire point: a silent backup failure is exactly
the gap this job exists to close, so any dump, upload, or prune error pages loudly rather than
being buried. Do not soften this to a report-inside-an-email model.

jobs.name: app-restore-jobsearch

[DR] Jobsearch Application Restore

Each Monday this job fetches the newest real jobsearch-*.sql.gz backup from the NAS, restores
it into a throwaway PostgreSQL server on the ephemeral Jenkins agent, and proves the restored application
data works. It complements the VM-level dr-restore job: that job proves a guest boots; this
one proves an application datastore restores with its expected schema and usable data.

Check | Evidence

Backup selection | Strictly selects the latest completed jobsearch dump, never a selfheal/studyguide dump or partial upload.

Isolation | Starts a fresh local PostgreSQL data directory with no TCP listener. The only scratch database is jobsearch_restore_test; production is never a target.

Restore | psql -v ON_ERROR_STOP=1 makes a corrupt or truncated dump red at the first SQL error.

Application assertions | Migration head 018, core tables, canary read, sane postings row band, and a fit-score foreign-key orphan check.

Evidence + teardown | Archives structured JSON and Prometheus exposition, stops the scratch server on every outcome, and fails if teardown fails.

Trigger: H 5 * * 1 (weekly Monday,
after the nightly DB backup). Agent: jobsearch. Failures mail through
standardPipeline notifyOn: 'failure'. The Jenkins exporter publishes
app_restore_success, duration, and last-success time; Prometheus alerts on a failed, stale,
or missing proof and Pyrra tracks the 28-day restore-success budget.

Controlled break:
CONTROLLED_BREAK=true replaces only the temporary fetched copy with invalid gzip bytes. The
NAS backup is unchanged. The attended acceptance build must turn red, retain teardown evidence, and exercise
the same alert/mail path the scheduled job uses. The stored and scheduled default is false.

Prerequisites: rebuild the
jobsearch-agent image so it contains PostgreSQL server binaries; keep the existing Vault

required.

jobs.name: site-traffic-collect

[Monitoring] Site traffic collector

Daily collector for the public sites. [private detail] serves no analytics beacon and its CSP is
script-src 'self', so nothing inside the page reports a visit. Cloudflare counts every
request at the edge instead, and this job pulls those counts into the aiops Postgres as
site_traffic_daily (one row per host per UTC day) and site_traffic_pages
(one row per host, day, path, browser and country) through
aiops/scripts/collect-site-traffic.py. Nothing is added to any page, no cookie is set and
no third-party script runs in a visitor's browser.

Why it has to run daily: on the Cloudflare free plan the detailed dataset is kept for about a week and one query may not span more than a day. A day that is never collected is gone for good once it ages out. A day that was missed can still be recovered with --days N inside that window, and every write upserts on a natural key, so a re-run corrects a day instead of doubling it. The very first build backfills by itself: with the tables empty the collector takes every day Cloudflare still holds rather than starting the history at today.

What this data cannot tell you: the free plan refuses clientRequestReferer and every bot-score field, so there is no referrer, no UTM attribution and no Cloudflare bot verdict. The human / non-human split stored beside each row is our own guess from the browser string; the raw browser value is kept so the rule can be revised and replayed over the history rather than lost at collection time.

Trigger: H 3 * * *. The collector asks for closed UTC days only, so it must run after 00:00 UTC; 03:00 clears that and stays out of the 06:00-08:00 block the aiops triage, backup digest and PBS collectors already occupy. Agent: jobsearch, the same agent as the other aiops collectors, for the Vault AppRole env and the hvac + psycopg2 deps. It also needs outbound HTTPS to [private detail], which is its one new requirement. Reads [private detail] and [private detail] from Vault at runtime (ADR-0010).

Green vs red (FAIL-LOUD): this job exists to persist, so a Cloudflare or DB failure exits non-zero and turns the build red. A silently skipped day would only surface later as a hole in a dashboard nobody was watching.

jobs.name: patch-estate
jobs.description:
Unattended Windows and Linux OS patching, including required reboots. Defaults to all updates during the Sunday 01:00-05:00 America/Denver admission window.

Every planned target must have a recent complete recovery point. PBS backups must be verified; Transit uses its independent Synology VMA archive and relay uses EBS snapshots. Missing backup evidence, incomplete inventory, active incidents or failed health checks stop the run.

Hosts patch one at a time. [private detail] must recover and both controllers must pass replication, DNS, LDAP and service checks before [private detail] starts. Vault quorum, hypervisor evacuation and Kubernetes readiness are checked where applicable.

REPORT_ONLY=true performs observation and backup checks without patching. There is no per-run approval prompt. Normal runs apply the authorized native-installer handoff before observation, including outside the patch window. This disables native automatic installation without installing updates or rebooting. Report-only runs leave update policy unchanged. Verified backup coverage remains mandatory before OS patching. An interrupted attempt blocks subsequent runs until recovery is verified.

Guests with generic Proxmox OS metadata require a read-only Ansible OS probe using existing SSH access. Unknown OS or failed discovery blocks the entire plan before host policy changes.

PVE reads verify both certificate chain and DNS identity using the committed cluster CA. Inventory failures name a phase and safe error category; incomplete discovery stops before update-policy adoption.

Relay access uses the existing control host's Tailscale connection and the provisioning SSH key. Both SSH host keys are pinned; failed access or changed keys block the run.

Linux update reporting preserves RPM and Debian package names and counts. Backup storage identity is checked through the read-only PVE storage listing with the existing token. Missing or mismatched storage and unverified recovery points block patching; retrieval errors report a safe context and category.

The existing job prepares encrypted PVE/PBS host configuration backups on Saturday at 10:00-10:59 Denver, then inventories and stages downloads before the separate patch workflow Sunday at 01:00-01:59. PREPARE_BACKUPS=true selects preparation manually and never enters patching. REPORT_ONLY=true prevents collection. Each host archive must pass authenticated decryption, byte comparison and PBS verification; a complete host rebuild remains a separate recovery exercise.

Every run archives a separate relay EBS audit before other backup checks. Preparation creates a crash-consistent snapshot set for every attached relay EBS volume when fresh coverage is missing, waits for completion and stops on failure before host collection. Pending snapshots are awaited without duplicate creation. Normal and report-only runs only audit EBS; failed evidence still blocks patch admission. Snapshots are retained, and a full relay restore remains untested. Preparation uses existing keys and pinned SSH; no new account or job is created. Backup, sync, GC and verification schedules were aligned on 2026-10-03 and read back with other settings preserved. Fresh verified recovery points and a successful admission run are still required before rollout is complete.

Runbook: Rolling estate patching.

VERIFY_MAINTENANCE_ADMISSION=true runs only the read-only guard checks for gvm-01 and ansible-control through the existing ansible SSH account, independent of the agent's local username. Unless RECOVER_BUILD_RUN is set, it overrides other mode selections and skips the entire estate workflow: no backup preparation, update-policy changes, package refresh, patching or reboot. Both rolling and native-policy results and their source revision are archived. Held claims are valid observations, never execution clearance. Missing or invalid evidence fails the build; successful observation does not prove autonomous disk growth.

The seed definition preserves the same Saturday preparation and Sunday patch triggers, all-update default, preparation parameter and build serialization as the Jenkinsfile.

Transit backup discovery and verification share the existing pinned primary-node SSH reader. The newest VM107 archive must be recent, complete, unchanged during verification and pass VMA integrity checks. No additional provisioning-token permission is required.

Update downloads are staged in bounded parallel batches before backup admission: STAGE_CONCURRENCY defaults to 5 (choices 1, 2, 5, 10). STAGE_ONLY=true downloads without installing, rebooting, creating backups or changing native policy; existing native installers must already be disabled. REPORT_ONLY prevents downloads, explicit PREPARE_BACKUPS remains backups-only, and VERIFY_MAINTENANCE_ADMISSION overrides other observation and estate modes; a nonempty RECOVER_BUILD_RUN selects recovery only.

Every selected host must complete staging. Receipts bind the host, request, scope and build; missing, stale or mismatched evidence blocks installation. Sunday repeats staging using host caches, then requires fresh complete verified backups and the maintenance window. Installation and reboot remain serial. Cache warming is not an offline guarantee: native installers may fetch newly applicable updates or evicted packages. A failed download stops the run. Staging artifacts include per-host receipts and staging.json.

Windows staging independently checks the Windows Update cache for every selected update ID. Already cached updates are accepted only when WUA reports them downloaded and uninstalled; missing IDs, incomplete downloads or search errors stop the build before receipts or installation.

Windows backup admission also requires a clean freeze/thaw task log for the exact verified snapshot. Before installation, all VSS writers must be healthy and retained event logs must show no VSS/Volsnap failure since that snapshot. Missing evidence blocks; no writers are reset automatically. DC diagnostics use DNS hostnames and a password-backed local runas logon for peer checks with the existing Vault credential. A backup repair and successful live diagnostics are still required before Windows rollout.

VERIFY_PLATFORM_READINESS=true observes both DCs with the existing password-backed runas health check, three Vault voters, three Ready Kubernetes nodes without pressure, and the RAM capacity necessary to evacuate each PVE node. It runs every check even if another fails and archives sanitized results with source hashes. Missing evidence or insufficient capacity fails the build. It creates no backups and performs no host mutation, package refresh or patching. VERIFY_MAINTENANCE_ADMISSION takes precedence; either verification mode excludes the estate workflow. A passing capacity bound is not a migration plan, drain test, storage-mobility test or patch authorization.

Before hypervisor patching, the admitted after-hours run pauses new builds, drains current work and gracefully parks seven dedicated build VMs after repeated backup checks. VM104's tunnel and the patch executor stay running. Autostart is suppressed temporarily. Guest migration spreads across destinations using the provisioning picker's measured RAM policy, cumulative disk checks and separation of DCs, Vault voters and K3s nodes. Guests return after host health passes, before advancing.

A persistent capacity journal records original power, autostart and admission states. Recovery runs after the PVE batch even on failure; unresolved capacity or guest placement keeps the journal. RECOVER_BUILD_RUN selects recovery only for its exact recorded build tag, including outside the maintenance window, and takes precedence over every other mode. It never patches. One-time ConfigMap/RBAC and existing-credential read grants must be applied before activation. Live shutdown, migration and recovery remain unverified until the controlled rollout.

jobs.name: pr-ci-dispatch
jobs.description:
[CI] Pull request dispatcher

[private detail]. Polls open automationlab pull requests on Gitea every two minutes and queues the
pr-ci runner for any immutable head SHA with no jenkins/pr-ci status, only a stale pending
reservation, or exactly one terminal failure/error. Success or two terminal failures stop dispatch for
that exact head, so infrastructure recovery is automatic but bounded to two attempts. This job and
pr-ci are ordinary
Job DSL Pipeline script from SCM jobs pinned to protected */main
(jenkins/jobs/pr_ci_jobs.groovy) - no Gitea branch-source plugin, no multibranch job, and
no PR content can ever change either job's own pipeline definition.

How it decides:
scripts/jenkins-pr-ci.py discover lists each open PR's head SHA, reads its Gitea commit
statuses, and emits a candidate when the jenkins/pr-ci context is absent, or is pending
and older than the stale threshold (default one hour - a runner that died mid-build without posting a
final status), or has exactly one terminal failure/error. It reads Gitea's plural
commit-status history endpoint so a fresh pending reservation cannot hide earlier failures. Before
queueing, this job writes a fresh pending reservation for that SHA so a second dispatcher run
within the same window does not queue a duplicate build. A success or a second terminal failure/error
ends retries for that exact SHA.

Concurrency: dispatcher runs remain serialized.
Each queued runner receives the PR's reviewed target branch (main or develop) along with its immutable head.
Discovery counts every fresh pending reservation as an active slot and queues only enough heads
to fill a global cap of four. The isolated pr-ci runners may overlap, so the queue drains without
an unbounded Kubernetes pod fan-out.

Trust boundary: this job passes only a validated
PR number and a validated 40/64-character hex SHA to pr-ci - never PR-controlled code or the
Gitea API token. It reads the repository with gitea-[private detail] and calls the Gitea status
API with the string credential gitea-jenkins-token; PR code runs in pr-ci's own
fresh pod and never receives either credential.

Schedule: H/2 * * * * on the prod
controller only - the DSL reads CONTROLLER_ENV and installs no cron trigger on dev, so dev
seeding the same jobs never polls or writes repository status. Gated end to end by
PR_CI_ENABLED (true in k8s/jenkins/jenkins-values.yaml, false in
values-dev.yaml): the "Discover untested PR heads" stage no-ops unless that flag is
true in the controller environment.

Apply and proof

Committed-not-applied; the guided apply/rollback procedure is
docs/ci-cd/364-multibranch-pr-ci-apply.md. Offline coverage (candidate selection, stale
reservation recovery, fail-closed SHA/PR-number validation) is
scripts/tests/test_jenkins_pr_ci.py.

jobs.name: Upgrade-Jenkins-Pipeline
jobs.description:
[Platform] Upgrade Jenkins

On-demand Helm re-apply of the Jenkins controller from its values file, so the running controller
always matches the declared config in git rather than accumulating undocumented UI changes. The
chart version is pinned to 5.9.26, so in practice this re-asserts configuration rather
than truly upgrading - bumping the pin is how a real upgrade is done. It is the job that
keeps the controller itself GitOps-managed, closing the "who changed Jenkins?" gap.

Schedule: None - on demand only. The weekly Sunday 02:00 cron (cron('0 2 * * 0')) was REMOVED from the Jenkinsfile by operator ruling on 2026-07-29, not merely disabled; re-enabling it is a documented, gated procedure (see the runbook's "Re-enabling the weekly schedule"). Agent: an inline Kubernetes pod with a standard jnlp (jenkins/inbound-agent) plus an alpine/k8s helm container carrying the jenkins-helm service account; the Helm stage runs in container('helm'). (The old label 'helm' template was broken - its only container was alpine/k8s named jnlp, no Jenkins agent, so pods never connected.)

What it does (stage by stage)

Stage | What it does, and why

Verify values present | Confirms k8s/jenkins/jenkins-values.yaml exists in the automationlab checkout ([private detail]: single source of truth - the item-05 recovered, Argo-managed copy in this repo), failing clearly rather than applying nothing. Replaces the old [private detail] curl.

Helm re-apply | helm repo add jenkins/update, then helm upgrade jenkins jenkins/jenkins -n jenkins --version 5.9.26 -f k8s/jenkins/jenkins-values.yaml. The explicit --version pin means the chart never moves on its own; the values file is re-applied so any drift from the declared config is corrected.

Parameters

None. It always re-applies the pinned chart with the current values file.

Failure & behavior

On every run the standard labNotify mails [private detail]
with subject [<result>] <job> #<n> - this replaced the bespoke
Jenkins Upgrade SUCCESS/FAILED emails when the job adopted the
standardPipeline shared library's helper (roadmap 1.3 wave 3, helpers-only: the job keeps its
declarative structure). No rollback: a failed helm upgrade leaves the previous release
in place (Helm keeps revision history), so the controller keeps running; investigate and re-run.
Note the controller upgrading itself can briefly restart the pod running this very build.

Note: Migrated from [private detail] and fixed ([private detail]): values now single-sourced from this repo (k8s/jenkins/jenkins-values.yaml) and mail routed to [private detail]. Still true: the chart is pinned to 5.9.26, so this re-asserts config and never actually upgrades - whether/when to bump the pin is an open policy decision (documented in the Jenkinsfile), not automated here. Before the first run from the new source, confirm the in-repo values file matches the currently-live config (the [private detail] copy was authoritative until now).

Source: jenkins/Jenkinsfile-upgrade-jenkins (uses the labNotify shared-library helper) | Runbook: docs/pipelines/upgrade-jenkins.md | Managed in git - edit the file, not this box.

jobs.name: cityamble-usage-collect
jobs.description:
[Monitoring] CityAmble usage collector

Hourly collector for CityAmble's Cloudflare Free plan limits and the app's own usage. It reads Worker requests, errors, CPU time and subrequests for trip-consumer-beta and trip-state-api, and D1 rows read, rows written and storage, from the Cloudflare GraphQL analytics API; and sign-ups, active accounts, affiliate clicks and route, search and weather outcomes from the Worker's own /api/v1/owner/metrics. It writes them as cityamble-usage.prom, archived on every build, through aiops/scripts/collect-cityamble-usage.py.

How it reaches Prometheus: the lab has no Pushgateway by design. The existing jenkins-success-exporter re-exposes the latest archived cityamble-usage.prom of this job, keeping only well-formed cityamble_* samples. Every capped series has a _limit companion with the same labels, so use versus cap is one division. The Grafana dashboard "CityAmble usage" and the CityAmble alert rules read those series.

Green vs red (NEVER RED FOR A SOURCE): a Cloudflare, Worker or Vault failure is recorded as cityamble_usage_source_up{source} 0 and the build stays green; the next hour recomputes everything. The alert CityAmbleUsageSourceDown fires after three hours at 0. A red build means the pipeline itself broke.

Trigger: H * * * *, hourly. Idempotent: every Cloudflare value is the current UTC day so far and every app value is the Worker's own total, so a rerun only refreshes the file. Agent: jobsearch (Vault AppRole env, hvac, outbound HTTPS to [private detail]; one new egress to [private detail]). Reads [private detail] (account [private detail] Analytics Read, D1 Read) and [private detail] (the Worker's USAGE_METRICS_TOKEN) from Vault at runtime (ADR-0010).

jobs.name: decommission-windows
jobs.description:
[VM] Decommission Windows

The Windows counterpart to the Linux teardown: it destroys the VM and reverses every provisioning
side effect, plus the two things a Windows host adds - the Active Directory computer
object and the per-host Zabbix PSK secret in Vault. It exists so a retired Windows
server leaves no orphaned AD object (which would otherwise linger in the Servers OU and confuse
audits), no ghost IP or DNS, no stale monitoring host, and no dead secret. The local-admin
password is deliberately kept for restore scenarios.

Schedule: On demand (Build with Parameters). Agent: provisioner pod for everything except AD + DNS Deregister, which hops to a windows agent.

What it does (stage by stage)

Stage | What it does, and why

Validate input | Trims/validates VM_NAME; it keys the workspace and the AD computer-object lookup.

Terraform Plan (destroy) | Selects the workspace, reads the real IP for later release, and stages a -destroy plan with is_windows=true so the shared Terraform module takes the Windows path.

Approval | Red HTML email to [private detail] (noting it also removes the AD object and DNS), then the gate: PERMANENTLY DESTROY Windows <name> (<ip>)?, button Destroy. The gate has a 30-minute timeout ([private detail]): no response aborts before Terraform Destroy, so nothing is destroyed.

Remove host manifest (runs before destroy) | gitCommitPush(remove:true) opens a jenkins-bot PR for inventory/host_vars/<name>.yml and blocks until it is durably auto-merged on main. The VMID/IP cannot be reused until the manifest is off main. A missing manifest is a no-op. If the merge fails, the stage fails and no VM is destroyed.

Terraform Destroy | Applies the approved destroy plan; the VM is gone after this. The manifest has already been durably removed before this stage runs.

Release IP from NetBox (if IP recovered) | netbox-release-ip.py returns the address to the pool.

Deregister Zabbix | zabbix-delete-host.py <name> removes the monitoring host.

Purge per-host Vault secrets | AppRole-logs in and vault kv metadata delete [private detail]<name> (|| true). The local-admin password is intentionally NOT purged - it is kept so a VM restored from PBS backup remains loginable.

AD + DNS Deregister (windows agent) | Finds the computer object by CN and DeleteTree()s it, bound via ADSI as the delegated [private detail] account (which holds Delete-Child on the Servers OU, scoping the permission narrowly). Then idempotently removes the A records in both zones and the reverse PTR.

Delete workspace | Deletes the empty per-VM Terraform workspace.

Parameters

Param | Meaning, default, consequence

VM_NAME | Hostname / Terraform workspace to destroy. Regex-validated. Also the CN used to find the AD computer object - a wrong name can destroy the wrong VM or match the wrong AD object.

Failure & rollback

post success: emails "Windows VM Decommissioned" (destroyed, removed from AD/DNS, IP released)
to [private detail]. post failure: emails "Windows VM Decommission FAILED"
with the build URL. No automated rollback; re-run to complete a partial teardown.

Note: Destructive and irreversible; it also DeleteTree()s the AD computer object as [private detail] (that account must keep Delete-Child on the Servers OU). The local-admin Vault password is deliberately retained for PBS restore - only the Zabbix PSK is purged; do not "clean up" the retained secret. AD lookup is by bare CN, so a duplicate CN could match the wrong object. Verify VM_NAME before approving.

Dev guardrail (ADR-0018): on the dev controller (CONTROLLER_ENV=dev) Terraform Destroy, Release IP from NetBox, Deregister Zabbix, Purge per-host Vault secrets, and AD + DNS Deregister are all skipped (plan-only); set APPLY_ON_DEV=true to run them for real. Prod runs every stage as normal.

Source: jenkins/Jenkinsfile-decommission-windows | Runbook: docs/pipelines/decommission-windows.md | Managed in git - edit the file, not this box.

jobs.name: provision-user
jobs.description:
[IAM] Provision User

End-to-end onboarding of a staff user across on-prem AD and Entra, driven by a role
definition so an operator supplies only identity fields and the correct OU, file-share groups,
mail distribution lists, cloud groups, and app tiles are provisioned consistently. It solves the
"new hire gets the wrong access because someone clicked through AD by hand" problem: the department
maps to a LabRole YAML that is the single source of truth for what that person gets.
Every step is idempotent, so re-running reconciles an existing user to their role.

Schedule: On demand. Agent: agent none - each stage pins its own (windows for AD, provisioner for Vault/Entra). The temp password crosses the Windows/Linux boundary only as a single-use Vault wrapped token, never as plaintext.

What it does (stage by stage)

Stage | What it does, and why

Validate SAM available (windows) | Validates the SAM format and checks AD. If the SAM already exists inside the managed Users OU it proceeds as an idempotent reconcile; if it exists elsewhere in AD it aborts - preventing collisions with unmanaged accounts.

Password → Vault + wrap (provisioner) | Generates a 24-char password, stores it at Vault [private detail]<SAM>, then re-reads it with a 15-minute single-use wrapped token passed forward. The plaintext never touches the Windows agent or the build log.

Load role (provisioner) | Parses iam/roles/<role>.yaml into flat env vars (OU, on-prem FS groups, mail DLs, Entra groups, app assignments). Centralizing YAML parsing here keeps the scripts taking simple arguments; the role YAML is the one source of truth for access.

AD user (windows) | Unwraps the token (which dies on use) to recover the password, then New-LabUser.ps1 creates or reconciles the AD account (DisplayName/UPN/mail/OU/Title/Dept, H: home drive on NASty, change-at-logon), sets the manager, and add-only reconciles the FS share groups and DL mail groups. On an existing user it never moves OU or resets the password.

Entra (provisioner) | entra-provision.py (app-only Graph creds from Vault [private detail] waits for AD Connect to sync the user into Entra (polls up to ~40 min, hard-fails if it never appears), then idempotently adds cloud groups and enterprise-app assignments so the My Apps tiles appear.

Parameters

Param | Meaning, default, consequence

SAM | sAMAccountName (e.g. jsmith), ^[a-z0-9.-]{2,20}$. Drives the UPN, account name, and temp-password path.

GIVEN_NAME / SURNAME | Set AD GivenName / Surname / DisplayName / CN.

DEPARTMENT | Service Desk / SysAdmin / Platform / NetOps. Maps to the LabRole YAML (service-desk/sysadmin/platform/netops) - this one choice determines OU, FS groups, mail DLs, Entra groups, and app tiles.

TITLE | Cascade dropdown filtered by DEPARTMENT; written to AD Title. Shows "select department first" until a department is chosen.

MANAGER_SEARCH / MANAGER | Type ≥2 chars to filter a live LDAP lookup (disabled accounts excluded), then pick. Sets AD Manager; a placeholder selection = no manager.

Failure & behavior

Only a post success block, which echoes how to retrieve the temp password
(vault kv get [private detail]<SAM>) for the manager, noting change-at-logon
is enforced. No failure notification and no rollback: a partial run (e.g. AD created but the
Entra sync timed out) leaves the AD account in place; recovery is to re-run, since every step is
idempotent. There is no approval gate.

Note: Idempotent - re-running reconciles an existing user to their role, but it only ADDS groups (never removes stale ones; that is deprovision's job) and never moves OU or resets the password. AD-mastered groups must be in the role's onPremGroups, not entraGroups (Graph returns 400 otherwise). The Entra stage can block up to ~40 minutes waiting for AD Connect; the wrapped token is single-use with a 15-min TTL, so a stalled/retried AD stage forces a restart from the wrap stage.

jobs.name: regen-derived-indexes
jobs.description:
[Platform] Regenerate derived indexes

Post-merge job that regenerates the three derived index files on main and commits the result,
ending the regen merge-race ([private detail]). Today every PR must commit docs/backlog/README.md,
docs/DOCS-INDEX.md, and grafana/data/milestone-data.json because the CI
--check gates require them - so any two in-flight PRs conflict on those three files, and a green
PR goes un-mergeable the instant a sibling lands, forcing a manual rebase + three-generator regen. This job
runs the generators on main after each merge and commits them, so PRs no longer need to carry the
regen (once the PR gates are relaxed - see the cutover doc).

Trigger: pollSCM('') - notifyCommit-only, self-healing, no webhook plugin (ADR-0008). The seed and Jenkinsfile both assert the same empty-schedule trigger, so re-seeding cannot clear it. It fires on every push to main; a guard skips the job's own [skip ci] regen commit so it cannot loop.

Commit path: gitCommitPush (the ADR-0007 bot lane) clones main, copies only the three named paths from the workspace, commits as jenkins-bot with [skip ci], and pushes with rebase-retry. Idempotent no-op when the three files already match main - so it is safe to enable BEFORE the PR gates are relaxed (while PRs still carry the regen, every run simply no-ops).

Agent: provisioner (git + Vault CLI + the AppRole env gitCommitPush needs). notifyOn: 'failure'.

Enabling (operator cutover)

The job's row is in the active JOBS list in jenkins/jobs/prod_jobs.groovy (landed 2026-08-31);
it is no longer staged in the commented block. The remaining cutover is sequenced in
docs/ci-cd/regen-derived-indexes-apply.md: (1) run the [Meta] Seed Jobs job to
materialize this job on the controller; (2) ADD the three derived paths to the Gitea branch-protection
bot-lane allowlist (else the bot push is rejected); (3) prove a no-regen PR self-heals; (4) only THEN
relax the three PR --check gates so PRs stop needing the regen. Each step is reversible.

jobs.name: entra-exporter-credential-rotation

Daily fail-closed 60-day rotation for the metadata-only Entra credential inventory exporter.

The job creates a 90-day replacement, CAS-updates only the registered Vault field, patches only the
existing monitoring/entra-credential-exporter Secret, and rolls out only its Deployment.
It validates Application.Read.All directly and requires the restarted exporter to report a
successful fresh inventory before starting a seven-day overlap. A failed validation restores both Vault
and the Kubernetes consumer to the prior value and retains both Entra credential IDs for recovery.

jobs.name: cert-sync
jobs.description:
[PKI] Certificate Sync

Keeps every deployed copy of *.[private detail] aligned with the sole cert-manager source,
default/Certificate wildcard-parsec-lab. The job updates six Kubernetes namespaces and
eight external endpoints, then verifies the certificate actually served on the wire. A mismatch or an
unreachable target fails the run; partial propagation is never reported as success.

Schedule: Monthly, 1st at 02:00 (0 2 1 * *). Also runnable on demand. Agent: the linux-tools Kubernetes pod, container tools.

What it does

Stage | Action and proof

Single-owner guard | Stops before fetching credentials if an independent argocd/Certificate wildcard-parsec-lab reappears.

Source validation | Reads the default/wildcard-parsec-lab-tls Secret, rejects a certificate inside 21 days of expiry, and proves the certificate and private key match.

Kubernetes fan-out | Updates the existing named Secret in argocd, jenkins, jenkins-dev, monitoring, nashville, and portal, then verifies Argo CD, Jenkins, Jenkins DEV, Grafana, Fleet, Nashville, Topology, and Portal from the wire. Nashville is checked at the Traefik origin because its public route correctly serves a separate Cloudflare edge certificate.

Ansible portals | Atomically installs and activates the certificate on Gitea, NetBox, Greenbone, and Wazuh with pinned SSH host keys, then requires an exact served-fingerprint match.

OPNsense | Updates one stable Trust certificate through a dedicated API identity, restarts only the WebGUI, and requires an exact served-fingerprint match.

Zabbix | Installs the pair under /etc/ssl/zabbix/ and reloads httpd.

Proxmox VE | Uses a forced-command helper to install only the custom pveproxy pair, restart the Web UI, and verify the exact source fingerprint on port 8006.

Proxmox Backup Server | Installs the pair under /etc/proxmox-backup/, restarts the proxy, and verifies the wildcard subject on port 8007.

Credentials and cleanup

SSH and OPNsense API identities are fetched from Vault only at runtime. The extracted TLS private key and all SSH key
files exist only in the ephemeral workspace and are removed by the pipeline's always hook.
Failures notify [private detail]; success is silent.

Verification: every destination must serve the exact source fingerprint. OPNsense uses normal CA validation after its one-time certificate selection and retains only the reviewed factory-leaf pin as a bootstrap fallback.

jobs.name: jenkins-api-token-rotation
jobs.description:
[IAM] Jenkins API Token Rotation

Automatically replaces the registered Jenkins automation API token every 60 days through Jenkins' supported per-user token API.

The replacement expires after 90 days. The job authenticates both tokens, CAS-updates Vault and the exact exporter Secret, proves the exporter is scraping, retains seven days of overlap, and revokes only the recorded predecessor UUID.

jobs.name: sync-backlog-issues
jobs.description:
[Backlog] Reconcile issues from item files

Reconciles the docs/backlog/NN-*.md item files against Gitea issues so the item files
are the single source of truth and no chat assistant has to mirror items to issues. Because
issues are derived from the committed files, a dead chat loses no tracking state. [private detail].

Trigger: the existing Gitea push webhook -> git plugin notifyCommit -> Poll SCM chain (no Gitea plugin), same as sync-public-site. The job self-filters to docs/backlog/ changes and no-ops otherwise. Agent: provisioner. On standardPipeline, notifyOn: 'failure'.

DRY_RUN parameter (UI, default TRUE): the stage defaults to dry-run when the parameter is absent, so it never makes a surprise live write. The first live run is a log-heavy backfill (~40 creates incl. 65-71, ~1 existing issue closed) - preview it with DRY_RUN checked, then uncheck to apply.

What it does

Action | When, and how

Create | No matching issue: create [NN] <H1>, body links the item doc path, labels mapped from the item's label line (tier-N->tier/N, theme/* where it exists; unmappable skipped and logged, never created). A new issue for a done item is closed in the same run.

Close | Item Status done and issue open: close with a comment referencing the doc.

Reopen | Item not done and issue was closed: reopen and log loudly.

It only creates / closes / reopens / comments / labels - never deletes an issue, never edits an item file. Idempotent: a second run with no doc change makes zero API writes. One loud log line per action.

Matching (authoritative, never a fuzzy guess)

Priority: (1) a canonical Issue: #NNN line in the doc; (2) an [NN] token in the issue title; (3) a docs/backlog/NN- reference in the issue body. Ambiguous at a tier -> skipped and logged. To point the reconciler at an existing differently-titled issue, add the canonical Issue: #NNN line to the doc.

Prereqs: Vault secret [private detail] (issue:write, version 2); the Vault AppRole env on the agent; python3 + Vault CLI on the provisioner; the UI job set up per the runbook (DRY_RUN param, Poll SCM verified-after-save, one manual Build Now baseline).

jobs.name: Sync-Grafana-Dashboards
jobs.description:
[Platform] Sync Grafana dashboards

Deploys the repo's Grafana dashboards into the kube-prometheus-stack Grafana via the
dashboard sidecar, replacing the manual "re-import the JSON in the Grafana UI after every
edit" step that let the dashboards go stale. For each committed, provisioning-ready
grafana/*.json it generates a ConfigMap labeled grafana_dashboard=1 in
namespace monitoring and applies it; the sidecar (METHOD=WATCH) live-reloads
Grafana. [private detail] (follow-up to [private detail]).

Run mode: Auto on merge - pollSCM('') (empty schedule, no cron) nudged by the Gitea notifyCommit webhook (ADR-0008, no plugin); a manual Build Now still works. No
approval gate - unlike Upgrade Prometheus, this only re-asserts committed dashboard JSON into
labeled ConfigMaps (no Helm release, CRD, or data is touched), so it is idempotent and safe to re-run.
Agent: an inline Kubernetes pod with a standard jnlp plus an alpine/k8s
kubectl container carrying the jenkins-helm service account; all cluster work
runs in container('kubectl') (the ADR-0006 in-cluster, unprivileged, scoped-ServiceAccount
posture).

What it does (stage by stage)

Stage | What it does, and why

Generate + enforce NOC overview ([private detail]) | In container('python'), gen-noc-overview.py --check regenerates the NOC overview from the scope/noc dashboards' domain/ + overview/primary tags and fails the build on any tag violation or if the committed noc-overview-dashboard.json is stale (drift). The repo is the sole source of truth (no /api/search).

Verify dashboards present | Confirms each wired grafana/*.json (jobsearch, pve-cluster, roadmap, noc-overview, litellm-gateway-budget) exists in the automationlab checkout, failing clearly rather than syncing nothing.

Validate JSON | If jq is present, asserts each wired file is valid JSON before it becomes a ConfigMap, so a malformed dashboard never ships.

Sync dashboards | For each dashboard, generates a grafana_dashboard=1-labeled ConfigMap straight from the committed JSON (kubectl create configmap --from-file --dry-run=client | kubectl label --local | kubectl apply) into monitoring. Stable name + apply = in-place update; the sidecar reloads Grafana. No committed ConfigMap, so the JSON is never duplicated.

Verify applied | Confirms the ConfigMap exists carrying the sidecar label and lists all grafana_dashboard=1 ConfigMaps in the namespace. (The sidecar reload is asynchronous WATCH, so this checks the apply, not the reload.)

WYSIWYG dashboards

The committed grafana/*.json are in provisioning form (concrete datasource uids, no export __inputs), so the sidecar loads them verbatim - what is in git is exactly what Grafana serves. A UI export produces export form with ${DS_...} placeholders; convert it back (strip __inputs/__requires, bake the uid) before committing.

Wired dashboards

Job Search (jobsearch-pg), Proxmox cluster (Prometheus ${datasource}), Roadmap (gitea-issues Infinity, [private detail]; its former jobsearch-pg burn-up panel was deleted 2026-08-03), and the generated NOC overview (grafana-dashboard-noc, Prometheus ${datasource}, [private detail]). The NOC overview deploys but its tiles render grey until alert rules carry domain=<name> labels and the phase-3 Zabbix datasource is wired - operator-verified-only ([private detail]). Deploy + light-up: docs/ci-cd/noc-overview-deploy.md.

Failure & behavior

On every run the standard labNotify mails [private detail] with subject
[<result>] <job> #<n>. The sync is idempotent; a failed apply leaves the
previous ConfigMap (hence the previously-synced dashboard) in place - fix and re-run. Concurrent builds
are disabled.

Prerequisites (the job does not create these): (1) RBAC - already satisfied: jenkins-helm can create/update ConfigMaps in monitoring via the helm-release-manager Role (k8s/monitoring/rbac/). No new RBAC. (2) Each dashboard's datasource must exist by uid - jobsearch uses jobsearch-pg, provisioned as code in k8s/monitoring/prometheus-values.yaml ([private detail]). Full detail: docs/ci-cd/sync-grafana-dashboards.md.

Source: jenkins/Jenkinsfile-sync-grafana-dashboards (uses the labNotify shared-library helper) | Runbook: docs/pipelines/sync-grafana-dashboards.md | Managed in git - edit the file, not this box.

jobs.name: estate-image-scan
jobs.description:
Estate image scan (weekly)

Discovery-driven vulnerability scan of the container images actually
running across the estate, not just the ones we build. Enumerates running images from the K3s API (all
namespaces) plus docker ps on the standalone Docker hosts, dedupes, Trivy-scans each, and emails a
by-severity report; a second stage LLM-triages the CRITICAL findings via the item-103 engine. Report-only.
[private detail] (Leg 1). Runbook: docs/pipelines/estate-image-scan.md.

Stage | What it does

Scan the estate's running images | kubectl get pods -A -o json → ansible docker_hosts ... docker ps --format json --tree → estate-scan/scripts/estate_image_scan.py: discover → normalize + dedupe running images → Trivy-scan each unique image → aggregate findings by severity → render JSON + Markdown + the backup-digest-style HTML email → land run coverage in security_scan_runs → archive + email. Also writes estate-critical.json (a merged, raw-Trivy-shaped report of just the CRITICALs) for the triage stage. Image metadata is untrusted data: escaped for the report, no execution path.

Triage CRITICAL findings ([private detail]) | security/scripts/scan-triage.py LLM-triages the CRITICALs (Ollama qwen2.5:7b, direct, keyless) into exploitable-vs-noise verdicts → archives triage-summary.md + triage.json. Scanner output is treated as untrusted DATA in a delimited block; verdicts are annotations only, no execution path.

File ai-triage issues ([private detail]) | security/scripts/file-ai-triage-issues.py files/reopens one Gitea ai-triage issue per exploitable finding in triage.json ([private detail] [private detail] via withLabVault - no new secret). First automated caller of the item-103 reconciler, feeding the item-98 GPU-decision labeled sample. No --close-resolved (this scan covers only running images, not the full repo).

File fixable findings ([private detail]) | Fixable, non-ignored CRITICAL findings are de-duplicated against the committed register and existing backlog. New findings open one ai/findings-vuln-* HOLD: PR for human review. The job never merges or writes main directly, and emails the filing digest.

Schedule H 4 * * 1 (weekly, Monday). The emailed report is the success signal. Fail-closed: a private image Trivy cannot pull, or Trivy missing entirely, is reported UNSCANNED (never silently clean) and marks the build UNSTABLE; the report is still emailed. A failed Docker-host inventory is named and lands INCOMPLETE; a reachable idle host is valid zero-image evidence. jobs.name: zabbix-cleanup-expired-maintenance
jobs.description:
[Ops] Zabbix Maintenance Cleanup

Daily janitor for the maintenance windows created by the on-demand maintenance job. A Zabbix
maintenance window stops suppressing when its end time passes, but the object itself lingers
forever - over weeks the maintenance list fills with dead entries that make it hard to
see what is actually being suppressed right now. This job deletes the expired ones so the list
stays honest. It only ever touches windows it can prove it created, so it can never remove a
long-running or manually-created window by accident.

Schedule: Daily, ~06:00 (cron('H 6 * * *'); H = per-job jitter within the hour). Also runnable on demand. Agent: a Kubernetes pod on the zabbix-agent image.

What it does (stage by stage)

Stage | What it does, and why

Cleanup Expired Maintenance | Logs in to the Zabbix API with an api_token from Vault [private detail] lists every maintenance window, and deletes only those that both start with the Jenkins-maintenance- name prefix and have an active_till in the past. The two conditions together are the safety rule: the prefix scopes deletion to this system's own windows, and the expiry check ensures an active window is never removed. Prints a count (or "No expired maintenance windows found").

Parameters

None. It is a fully automatic reconcile with no knobs.

Failure & behavior

No rollback (deletion of an already-expired window is not reversible and not harmful). The job
emails [private detail] on every run outcome (notifyOn: 'always'):
this is a scheduled cron whose failure is otherwise silent, so the daily mail doubles as a dead-man
heartbeat - its absence, or a FAILURE subject, is the signal. If the Zabbix API is down the login
fails and the build errors; the next daily run catches up. It never deletes an active window, so a
missed run only leaves husks, never breaks suppression.

Note: Only removes windows created by the maintenance job (the Jenkins-maintenance- prefix) that have already expired. Windows created by other means, or still active, are left untouched by design.

jobs.name: digest-dms-heartbeat
jobs.description:
[Monitoring] Digest dead-man's-switch heartbeat sender

The sender half of the digest dead-man's-switch ([private detail] follow-up). Every ~15 minutes it reads
each daily digest's heartbeat age (hours since its last successful send) from the aiops Postgres
and pushes each value to a Zabbix trapper item, where a pre-created trigger pages when the
age exceeds ~30h - a missed digest. Watches two digests: the backup digest
(digest.dms.backup.age) and the AIOps triage digest (digest.dms.aiops.age).

Why a push, not an ODBC pull: the aiops Postgres (postgres.terraform-state) is ClusterIP-only, unreachable from the VLAN-10 Zabbix VM, so the watcher runs in-cluster and pushes outbound to Zabbix :10051 - the item-88 / noc-reconcile.py pattern. Postgres stays unexposed; no zabbix_ro role, no ODBC DSN. It does not depend on the digests, so it detects their absence.

Trigger: cron('H/15 * * * *') (every ~15m, so the >30h trigger has fresh data). Agent: jobsearch (Vault AppRole env + psycopg2). On standardPipeline (labNotify); notifyOn: 'failure'. Reuses the aiops DB role ([private detail] - no new credential.

Green vs red: the trapper values are the alert surface - a Zabbix trigger owns the page - so the build stays green once both are sent. It goes red only on an operational failure (cannot read the aiops DB or reach Zabbix), meaning the value is stale and must be fixed. A never-run digest is not a red build; it is a large pushed age (999999) that trips the trigger.

Committed-not-applied. Does nothing useful until the operator (per docs/monitoring/digest-dead-mans-switch.md) creates the digest-dms Zabbix host, the two trapper items digest.dms.backup.age / digest.dms.aiops.age and their >30 and nodata() triggers, reuses the item-19 email action, and sets ZABBIX_SERVER. Until then a run fails loud, never a silent all-clear.

jobs.name: website-security-scan
jobs.description:
[Security] Public website scan

Weekly, report-only assessment of the four committed
[private detail] public origins. It crawls the public sitemap, verifies headers, redirect and
Cloudflare Access boundaries, checks DNS hygiene, exposed files, certificate expiry and all four bounded catalog checks,
then normalizes a rate-limited signed-template Nuclei scan. Runbook:
docs/pipelines/website-security-scan.md.

Stage | Contract

Research | Reads four HTTPS-allowlisted official sources and asks local Ollama for bounded advisory context. The research spotlight rotates by ISO week; all four committed catalog checks run every week. Model text cannot become commands, URLs, payloads, or remediation.

Signed Nuclei | Downloads checksum-pinned Nuclei v3.11.1, clones fresh official templates, rejects unsigned templates, excludes intrusive/fuzz/brute-force and active code/headless protocols, and caps traffic at 8 requests/second.

Deterministic scan | Runs exact-scope HTTP, sitemap, CORS, access-boundary, DNS, deployment-file, TLS trust/expiry, and all four safe-method checks; normalizes duplicate scanner matches; writes JSON, Markdown, and JUnit.

Publish | Archives provenance, JSON, Markdown, JUnit, and the backup-digest-style HTML email; lands run coverage in security_scan_runs; and emails the HTML digest to [private detail]. The digest links to Grafana and this build.

Schedule
H 6 * * 6 (weekly, Saturday). Findings are advisory. An unreachable target, missing report,
invalid input, incomplete sitemap coverage, unavailable research source, or failed scanner is loud and marks the build UNSTABLE; a report
is still preserved when possible. No login attempts, brute force, state-changing requests, generated exploit
payloads, automatic remediation, Vault secret, or Docker daemon.

Internal sites are a separate proposed profile in the runbook; they are not enabled by this job.

jobs.name: upgrade-loki
jobs.description:
[Platform] Upgrade Loki

Executable, auditable upgrade / re-apply of the Loki Helm release (loki in namespace
monitoring) from the values file tracked in git (k8s/monitoring/loki-values.yaml).
Mirrors Upgrade Prometheus exactly: a diff preview, a manual approval gate, and a post-upgrade
rollout check, wrapping the helm upgrade --install that stands the log-aggregation backend
up. [private detail]. Guided apply: docs/monitoring/loki-deploy.md.

Run mode: On demand (NOT scheduled). Like
Upgrade Prometheus, the upgrade gates behind manual approval, so an unattended schedule would only
stall at the gate. Agent: an inline Kubernetes pod with a standard jnlp
(jenkins/inbound-agent) plus an alpine/k8s helm container carrying the
jenkins-helm service account; all cluster work runs in container('helm') (the
ADR-0006 in-cluster, unprivileged, scoped-ServiceAccount posture).

What it does (stage by stage)

Stage | What it does, and why

Validate pinned chart version | Fails LOUD before any helm command if CHART_VERSION is empty. Loki is a NEW release with no in-use pin, and an empty --version makes helm resolve LATEST (the revision-13 defect upgrade-prometheus hit). A shell ${CHART_VERSION:?} backstop guards the later stages too.

Verify values present | Confirms k8s/monitoring/loki-values.yaml exists in the checkout, failing clearly rather than applying an empty/default release.

Preview (diff / plan) | Adds the grafana Helm repo, then shows what the upgrade would change before anything is applied - the validation gate for chart-version-specific keys (the Loki chart shifted keys 5.x -> 6.x). Uses helm diff upgrade if the plugin is present; otherwise helm template (proposed) vs helm get manifest (live) as a unified diff (indicative, not exact).

Approve upgrade | Manual input gate after the preview (confirm retention + PVC size). Nothing has changed in the cluster up to this point.

Helm upgrade | helm upgrade --install loki grafana/loki -n monitoring --version <CHART_VERSION> -f k8s/monitoring/loki-values.yaml. The explicit --version pin means the chart never moves on its own; --install makes the first run stand the release up.

Post-upgrade rollout check | kubectl -n monitoring rollout status statefulset/loki --timeout=300s (SingleBinary mode renders a StatefulSet). A stuck rollout fails the build, so a broken upgrade is loud.

Parameters

CHART_VERSION - the grafana/loki chart version to apply. No default on purpose - the operator sets the exact version confirmed to resolve on [private detail] (docs/monitoring/loki-deploy.md); an empty value is refused.

Failure & behavior

On failure the standard labNotify mails [private detail]
([<result>] <job> #<n>). No rollback: a failed helm upgrade
leaves the previous revision running (Helm keeps history) - investigate and re-run, or
helm rollback loki <rev> -n monitoring to revert deliberately. Concurrent builds are
disabled so two upgrades cannot race.

Prerequisites (the job does not create these): (1) RBAC - already satisfied by the existing k8s/monitoring/rbac/helm-release-manager.yaml Role ([private detail]), which grants jenkins-helm the namespaced objects a Loki single-binary release ships; Loki has no cluster-scoped admission webhooks, so no extra cluster grant is needed. (2) A default StorageClass for the SingleBinary PVC (confirm the size against cluster storage, [private detail] retention fork). Full detail: docs/monitoring/loki-deploy.md.

jobs.name: cloudflare-credential-rotation
jobs.description:
[IAM] Cloudflare Credential Rotation

Daily lifecycle job for the Cloudflare account-owned DNS and Access IdP updater tokens, the user-owned public-site cache-purge token,
their separate alternating credential-manager pairs, and metadata-only Access service-token inventory.

Each managed token is replaced every 60 days with a 90-day credential, validated against
its exact registered API resource, retained alongside its predecessor for seven days, and then retired
by exact provider ID. Two narrowly scoped manager tokens roll each other so a lost
one-time response remains recoverable. Access tokens are inventoried but are not called
automatic unless their complete consumer cutover is controlled.

Safety: the worker uses Vault CAS, never prints token values, changes
no DNS record or cached content, and cannot administer any Cloudflare capability outside the registered
API-token and Access service-token lifecycle paths.
